measurements:
I measured open item O1, `delegate_index_bound`, in a patched copy of the ZKP4 prototype. Files: scratchpad/review-soundness/vc/src/proxy_delegation/circuit.rs and circuit/tests.rs, built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=scratchpad/review-soundness/target. The patch adds public input 11 (`bound`), witnesses a = d-1 and b = bound-d, adds two AddChip equalities (a+1 = d, b+d = bound), and adds two strict 4-word (40-bit) lookup range checks. Slot nullifier C14 is still present.

Results on an M3 Ultra (release, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8, host load average about 17):
- **Rows:** CircuitCost k=11, max_rows=2015/2048, unchanged from the prototype whether the range checks are on the primary track or on track B. `Circuit::default()` also gives 2015 rows, so witness independence holds. Columns: 34 advice, 78 fixed, 4 lookups.
- **Real proof:** keygen 134 ms; proof 11,008 B; median prove 98 ms over 8 runs; verify about 1.7 ms.
- **MockProver:** d = bound passes; d = bound+1 is rejected; d = 0 is rejected; d = bound = u32::MAX passes. All 13 original prototype tests still pass.

No chain-side prototype was run. The routing and identity-C1 analysis relies on the existing proto-chain/route_test.go plus a code reading of curvey ScalarPallas.Hash (expand_message_xmd with BLAKE2b, deterministic).
confirmations: No double spend across circuits: ZKP2 and ZKP4 share one VAN nullifier. Both compute Poseidon4(nk, "vote authority spend", round, van_old) and both go into set 0x01 (proto circuit.rs:499-518; vc vote_proof C5). A VAN is either cast from or delegated from, never both.

Nothing can create VC(0, d) or open a DC as a vote, and there are two independent barriers. (1) The ZKP2 non-zero gate (authority_decrement.rs:398-416). (2) The chain rejects proposal_id < 1 for casts (msgs.go:139-141; ValidateProposalId keeper_voting.go:255-264). ZKP4's proposal slot and DOMAIN_VC are fixed constant cells (proto circuit.rs:706-731). VAN leaves (Poseidon2) cannot collide with VC/DC leaves (Poseidon5). ZKP3 binds (p, d) publicly into the VC hash.

Field wrap is ruled out. ZKP1 bounds W to [1, 2^30] (delegation/circuit.rs:1361-1375). ZKP4 range-checks W_new strictly below 2^30 (proto :564-570), checks each share strictly below 2^30 (:607-615) and requires w != 0 (:602-605). Together these give W = w + W_new over the integers.

Pools are never decrypted or completeness-checked. CollectNonEmptyAccumulators (keeper_tally.go:307-319), ValidateEntryBounds (keeper_voting.go:291-304), the partial-decryption injector (prepare_proposal_partial_decrypt.go:153), BSGS tally and roundHasAccumulators (prepare_proposal.go:282,352) and ProcessProposal (process_proposal.go:172,234) all iterate round.Proposals or require p >= 1.
Genesis export walks the whole TallyKey and ShareCount prefixes (keeper/genesis.go:477-511,559-598), so pool accumulators survive export and import.

Pools are final when routing runs. The transition block cannot admit reveals or routes: ValidateRoundForVoting rejects blockTime >= vote_end_time (keeper_voting.go:336-338), and reveals refuse TALLYING (msgs.go:554-557). Routing at the ACTIVE->TALLYING EndBlock (module.go:491-512) therefore sees final pools. Partial decryptions are injected only from the next block, against routed state.

The re-randomizer is deterministic and closes the identity-C1 attack. Forcing final.C1 to the identity requires sum(r) = -H(round, p, o, combined), a hash fixed point. The partial-decryption DLEQ rejects only an identity C1 (dleq.go:95-96).

Routed buckets stay decodable: each lineage contributes at most W0 per proposal, so every bucket total is at most 1.68e8 ballots, below TallyBSGSBound = 2^28 (keys.go:33-35). Nothing is ever subtracted.

The slot nullifier cannot be bypassed in the circuit. nk and rand are the same cells used in C2, C3, C5 and C6 (proto :520-543), so rand cannot change along a chain. rand is per bundle, derived from bundle_index and the note set (van_blinding.rs:38-92). The nullifier is bound to the round, and the tag+slot field never collides with the VAN tag. Holding several bundles yields at most 16 DCs per registration.

Duplicate VAN nullifiers inside one batch cannot arise from valid proofs, because w != 0 and the authority decrement make every successor distinct. For 0x06 and 0x07 ValidateBasic already rejects them (msgs.go:180-205), so the only gap is the new slot set (SND-1).

No delegator can redirect or block another delegator's DC. Share nullifiers bind the DC and exclude p and d, so each share is added at most once. A DC cannot be duplicated without the full opening, including the El Gamal randomness. Griefing via AddToTally's identity check (keeper_tally.go:72-75) needs the discrete log of the victim's C1.
Route replay fails: routes are one-shot per (round, d, p) in state, all-or-nothing, and the digest binds round_id and key_epoch. Chain binding is the remaining gap (SND-3).

The 256-reveals-per-block cap covers pool reveals unchanged (vote_share_submission_proposal.go:96-121). It runs ValidateBasic inside ProcessProposal, so the p=0 branch must be identical on all validators, which the coordinated halt already provides.

findings.title: The DC slot nullifier (the 16-DCs-per-chain DoS bound) is in the integrated doc but missing from the chain/ZIP contracts and from the shared ante and genesis code paths
findings.description: The integrated design adds `dc_slot_nf` as ZKP4 public input 10 and a new nullifier set 0x03 (integrated-design-v1.md:69-70,107,109). Nothing else carries it through. The chain spec, which the integrated doc names authoritative for detail, has no slot nullifier anywhere: its `ProxyDelegationAction` has no `dc_slot_nf`, D1 omits it, and the ante steps and handler never check or set it. The ZIP-PD statement goes further and replaces the slot nullifier with a public `min_dc_ballots`. Today's shared code paths also cannot hold a fourth set. Genesis validation rejects nullifier types above 2. The generic ante nullifier step checks one set per message, plus a hard-coded special case for the 0x07 composite. `CheckNullifiersUnique` only checks the store and does not dedupe within a list.

[code] x/vote/types/genesis.go:94-97 (`nullifier_type > 2` is rejected); x/vote/ante/validate.go:119-135 (one type per message via `GetNullifierType`, plus the 0x07 special case at :123-128); x/vote/keeper/keeper_voting.go:54-66 (store-only check); msg_server.go:246-250 (handlers use `SetNullifier`, not CheckAndSet).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) The implementer follows chain.md: ZKP4 is verified with the client-supplied `dc_slot_nf`, but the value is never recorded. A VAN chain of W ballots can then mint up to W DCs at 10 per tx (w>=1 each); 8,000 ballots gives 8,000 DCs and 128,000 fee-less reveal txs, against a cap of 16 DCs (256 reveals). (b) The slot nf is recorded with `SetNullifier` and checked only by the generic ante step, which keys on one type. The slot set is never checked in CheckTx or RecheckTx, so the same slot is reused across txs. (c) Slot nfs are recorded correctly, but `ValidateGenesis` is left unchanged. The next export/import fails with "nullifiers[i].nullifier_type is 3, expected 0-2", so the chain cannot restart from an exported genesis.
findings.proposed_fix:
Make the integrated doc normative for the slot nullifier:
- Wire: add `dc_slot_nf` to `ProxyDelegationAction`.
- D1: bind it.
- ValidateBasic: reject duplicate slot nfs and duplicate VAN nfs within the message, as `MsgCastVoteBatch` already does (msgs.go:180-205).
- Ante step 4, in CheckTx and RecheckTx: check gov (0x00, when a registration is present), VAN (0x01) and slot (0x03), as an explicit special case like validate.go:123-128.
- Handler: CheckAndSet all three sets before any write.
- Genesis: accept type 3 in `ValidateGenesis` and in export.
- Queries and docs: add type 3 to the `nullifier/{round}/{type}/{nf}` enum and to the IAVL key docs.
- ZIP-PD: delete `min_dc_ballots`, or state explicitly that it is replaced by C14.

verdict.reasoning:
The cited gaps are real, but the finding misreads which document governs, and it overstates the consequences.

**What the integrated doc already settles.** It is allowed to override the component specs (integrated-design-v1.md:3), and it already makes the slot nullifier normative:
- `dc_slot_nf` is in the `ProxyDelegationAction` wire (:107).
- The single batch digest covers it (:106).
- Slot nfs go to a new set 0x03 (:109).
- Intra-message duplicates are rejected for all sets (:109).

The circuits spec states the same chain contract (circuits.md:306, 558). So scenario (a), where an implementer follows chain.md and never records the slot nf, means ignoring an explicit override. It is drift between documents, not a missing design.

**What is genuinely missing.** Neither the integrated doc nor the chain spec says where set 0x03 is checked. The generic ante step checks one type per message (validate.go:119-131), with a hand-written case only for 0x07 (:123-128), so 0x09 needs its own explicit case covering gov, VAN and slot. Also missing:
- the handler's check-then-set for 0x03;
- `ValidateGenesisState` accepting type 3 (genesis.go:94-97);
- the chain FFI inputs struct and packing (chain.md:731-740);
- chain D1 (chain.md:340-346);
- ZIP-PD, which uses `min_dc_ballots` instead (spec_rollout.md:124-127, 141-156, 164-165);
- the client builder, which has no `dc_slot` parameter (client.md:254-261).

**Overstated consequences.**
- Scenario (c), genesis: `InitGenesis` never calls `ValidateGenesisState` (module.go:686-708). Import writes any type (keeper/genesis.go:105-110), and export iterates the whole 0x01 prefix (keeper/genesis.go:380-409). Only the `genesis validate-genesis` CLI would fail. The repo scripts run it on the canonical launch genesis, which holds no nullifiers. So "the chain cannot restart" becomes a loud, trivially fixed CLI rejection on an emergency export path.
- Scenario (b), ante: if the handler checks 0x03, a reused slot only wastes one mempool ZKP4 verification and then fails in DeliverTx.
- The DoS bound itself: each ZKP2 cast and each ZKP4 DC yields exactly 16 reveals per attacker proof. A 1-ballot registration can already drive 50×16 = 800 reveals. An attacker who splits notes before the snapshot already beats the uncapped DC path per ZEC (chain.md:607-610). The cap is useful defense-in-depth against a single-note whale, but losing it does not create a new class of DoS. This is not medium or high.

findings.title: Consensus-critical encodings disagree across the specs: ZKP4 public-input layout, leaf append order, batch sighash, route digest and pool share counting
findings.description:
Five encodings that every implementation must match byte for byte have two or three incompatible definitions:
1. **ZKP4 public-input order.** Circuits and integrated put `dc_slot_nf` at offset 10 with the bound open. The chain FFI puts `delegate_index_bound` at 7 with no slot nf. ZIP-PD puts `min_dc_ballots` at 7.
2. **Leaf append order.** Integrated, chain and client use [final VAN, c1..cn]. ZIP-PD uses DC leaves, then VC leaves, then the final VAN.
3. **Batch sighash.** Chain D1 omits `recovery_hint` and `dc_slot_nf` but includes the bound. The client's `SVOTE_PROXY_CAST_BATCH_SIGHASH_V1` uses different domains, adds `n_proxy`/`n_vote` and the hint, and omits the slot nf. Integrated says one digest covers everything, including the hint and the slot nf.
4. **Route digest.** Chain D7 binds `lp8(chain_id)` and `key_epoch`. The identity spec binds `key_epoch` but no chain or network. ZIP-PD binds chain_id and `dk_pubkey` but no `key_epoch`.
5. **Pool share count.** The chain calls `IncrementShareCount(0,d)`, ZIP-PD says it MUST NOT, and integrated adds a separate `PoolShareCount`.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:69-72,106,108,131; chain.md:143,185,340-346,357,740; circuits.md:73-85; spec_rollout.md:141-156,195,200,217,245; client.md:273-278,457; identity.md:203. [code] internal/helper/api.go:663-677 (the helper rejects a payload whose recomputed `vcHash` does not equal the leaf at `tree_position`).
findings.failure_scenario: A wallet that implements ZIP-PD (a third-party wallet, or Zodl later) computes DC positions as DCs-first. Its helper payloads carry the wrong `tree_position`. `verifyCommitment` returns ErrInvalidCommitment (a permanent rejection), the shares are never revealed, and the DC weight is stranded with no recovery. Separately, a client/chain sighash mismatch makes every 0x09 fail signature verification, and a public-input order mismatch makes every ZKP4 fail verification. Both are total liveness failures for proxy delegation in that release.

verdict.reasoning:
The documents do disagree. But the integrated doc, which may override the components, already resolves three of the five items, and the failure scenarios are overstated.

**Item 2, leaf order.** Settled: integrated :108 says "final VAN, then commitments in action order (as today)". The chain spec agrees (chain.md:143), as do the current code (msg_server.go:251-262) and the client (client.md:457). Only the ZIP-PD outline is wrong (spec_rollout.md:200).

**Item 5, pool share count.** Settled: integrated :131 says a separate `PoolShareCount` and never `ShareCount`. ZIP-PD's "MUST NOT IncrementShareCount" is consistent with that. Only chain.md:185 is stale.

**Item 1, public-input order.** Settled for order: integrated :69-70 matches circuits.md and the prototype (circuit.rs:75-86). The chain FFI is told to build the instance through voting-circuits' own constructor and never hand-order fields (chain.md:737), so the remaining gap is content (slot nf; the bound is open item O1). That duplicates SND-1. ZIP-PD's `min_dc_ballots` is an unadopted alternative.

**Items 3 and 4 are genuinely unresolved at byte level.**
- Item 3, batch digest: integrated says one digest covers everything, including the hint and slot nf, but gives no layout. The only byte-level definitions are chain D1 and D2 (chain.md:340-347). Those were written for the two-tag design and omit `recovery_hint`. The client sketch differs, but the client explicitly defers to the chain (client.md:271 "The chain owns these").
- Item 4, route digest: integrated never defines it. Chain D7 (chain.md:357) has `lp8(chain_id)`, `writeU32As32` and a u64 `key_epoch`. identity.md:203 has u32le fields, a u32 `key_epoch` and no `net`; it is labelled a contract "offered to the chain". ZIP-PD :245 binds `dk_pubkey` and has no epoch.

The integrated design's single tag with optional registration and its DIK/DRK registry make chain D2-D7 obsolete, so these two digests must be written fresh.

**Overstated failure scenarios.**
- Sighash and public-input mismatches would surface in the golden-vector and e2e tests the chain test plan already requires ("Golden vectors for D1–D7, shared with e2e sighash.rs"), not in production.
- Wallets do not compute leaf positions from a layout rule. They take them from event attributes (zcash_voting confirmation.rs:19-20), or they match the expected leaf sequence by value during exact-tree recovery (recovery.rs:406-411). A wrong order gives NoMatch, not wrong positions. The wallet-API ZIP has wallets locate leaves by syncing the tree.
- A helper `ErrInvalidCommitment` (api.go:684-686) can be resubmitted with the correct position until `vote_end_time`, so "stranded with no recovery" does not hold.

The real, narrower point: the hint is not a ZKP4 public input. If an implementer follows chain D1, which the integrated doc names authoritative for detail, the hint is unsigned. A relayer or proposer could then swap it and silently break R1/R2 recovery for that DC.

verdict.refined_fix:
Keep the fix narrow. Only the unresolved items need new definitions.

(a) **Batch digest.** Add one byte-level D1 to integrated §4.1 for the single-tag 0x09. It uses the chain's existing `write32`/`writeU32As32`/`writeU64As32` idiom and binds, in order:

(d) **Golden vectors.** Extend the planned golden vectors to the new D1 and the route digest. Share them across Go, e2e `sighash.rs`, zcash_voting and the `zcash_vote_delegate` crate.

findings.title: Open item O1 resolved by measurement: `delegate_index_bound` fits at K=11 with no row growth; adopt it
findings.description: Without the bound, d is an unconstrained private field element. A DC can target an index that does not exist yet. The chain accepts the DC, and then the weight is either stranded (the helper rejects it permanently, the chain rejects the reveal) or captured by whoever is assigned that index later. The integrated doc kept the bound only "if it still fits at K=11". I added it to a copy of the prototype ZKP4, which already contains C14, as public input 11. The constraints are a = d-1 and b = bound-d, two AddChip equalities (a+1 = d, b+d = bound), and two strict 4-word (40-bit) lookup range checks. 40 bits is sufficient: a, b < 2^40 and a+b+1 = bound < 2^32 force integer equality, so 1 <= d <= bound. This removes failure mode 5 in chain.md §7 and the helper's permanent unknown-index path. Caveat: the bound is public, so clients must all use the same value. The chain-advertised `NextDelegateIndex-1` at a recent checkpoint works. A client's own directory-snapshot maximum would fingerprint when it fetched the directory and link its DCs.
findings.evidence: [measured] Patched copy: scratchpad/review-soundness/vc/src/proxy_delegation/circuit.rs (C15 block before C13) and circuit/tests.rs (review_* tests). CircuitCost: k=11, max_rows=2015, the same as without the bound, whether the range checks sit on the primary track or on track B. `Circuit::default()` gives the same 2015 rows. Instance has 12 public inputs. Real keygen, prove and verify all pass: proof 11,008 B, median prove 98 ms (8 threads, host load ~17), verify ~1.7 ms. MockProver: d = bound passes, d = bound+1 fails, d = 0 fails, d = bound = u32::MAX passes, and all 13 original prototype tests still pass. [doc] chain.md:597 (stranded-weight path without the bound); integrated-design-v1.md:72.
findings.failure_scenario: Without the bound: a buggy or compromised directory, or a race on a wallet's view of the registry, produces DC(d = NextDelegateIndex + k). The tx lands and the VAN weight w is consumed. The helper returns a permanent ErrInvalidRoundChoice, so the weight is lost. If index d is registered later, whoever registers it receives those delegations whenever the shares are revealed.
findings.proposed_fix: Adopt the bound. Make it a u32 public input (offset 11, or reorder per SND-2). The chain rejects `bound >= NextDelegateIndex` in ante and handler. The client must use a chain-advertised common bound, never its own snapshot maximum. Add the four review_* MockProver cases to the circuit test plan.

findings.title: With the optional registration folded into 0x09, the chain must pick action 0's root by whether a registration is present, never by `anchor_height`, or a front-runner can burn a victim's registration
findings.description: The ZKP1 spend-auth signature covers only the tx1 effects (validate.go:259-274), so a registration lifted from the mempool is valid in any envelope. The composite rule never appends van_cmx (msg_server.go:286-289,323-327). Suppose an implementation of the merged tag selects the first root from `anchor_height` (0 means synthetic, otherwise a real root) instead of from whether a registration is present. Then a message with a registration plus a nonzero anchor verifies action 0 against the real tree. Today's 0x07 cannot hit this: ValidateBasic forces anchor 0 (msgs.go:228-233) and verification always uses SingleLeafRoot(van_cmx) (validate.go:218-225). The integrated text states the intended rule ("with a registration, synthetic anchor 0") but does not require rejecting the mixed form.
findings.evidence: [code] x/vote/ante/validate.go:218-225,259-274; x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:312-327; x/vote/types/msgs.go:228-233. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:100-105; spec_rollout.md:181-182.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker sees the victim's 0x09 (registration + DCs) in the mempool. They submit their own 0x09 carrying the victim's registration (valid on its own) plus one tiny cast from the attacker's own tree VAN with a real anchor. The chain sets the victim's gov nullifiers, verifies the attacker's action against the real root, and appends the attacker's leaves; the victim's van_cmx is never appended. The victim's notes can no longer register this round, so their whole registered weight is lost.
findings.proposed_fix: ValidateBasic: require `anchor_height == 0` when a registration is present and `!= 0` when it is absent. Every nested cast must carry the batch anchor. Ante and handler derive root0 from whether the registration is present. D1 binds a has_registration byte plus van_cmx. Add a negative e2e test: "registration + real anchor is rejected".

findings.title: Identity-spec route and registry digests bind no chain id (route) or only `net` (registry ops), so routes, freezes and terminal revokes can replay across vote chains on the same network
findings.description: The identity spec signs `route` over `round_id, index, key_epoch, n, entries`, with no chain or network binding. Registry ops (`rotate_route`, `freeze`, `revoke`, `cancel_pending`) bind `net` = "main"/"test"/"regtest" rather than the vote chain id. The chain spec's D3-D7 use `lp8(chain_id)`, but the integrated doc does not say which digests win (see SND-2). Several vote chains can share one Zcash network: the isolated rehearsal chain `upgrade-test-1` is one, and a re-genesis from an export is another. After an export, the registry indices and `key_epoch`s are identical. round_id depends only on creation height and round content, so a cloned chain that replays a create action at the same height gets the same round_id.
findings.evidence: [doc] identity.md:186-203 (`net` encoding; `route` digest without net or chain), identity.md:116 (freeze), identity.md:112-119 (revoke is terminal); chain.md:338,357. [code] app/isolated_rehearsal_upgrade.go:15-19 (a separate-network chain); x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:401-413 (round_id inputs).
findings.failure_scenario: A delegate uses the same delegate phrase on a rehearsal or staging chain whose registry state was cloned from production, and revokes or freezes there while testing. Anyone replays that signed `revoke` on the production vote chain: same net, index and key_epoch. The entry becomes REVOKED, which is terminal, and every un-routed proposal of its committed pool abstains.
findings.proposed_fix: Prefix every DIK/DRK digest (route, rotate, change, recover, cancel, freeze, revoke) and the verifier attestation with `lp8(chain_id)`, as chain.md D3-D7 already do. Keep `net` only for off-chain display statements.

findings.title: A stolen hot DRK can irreversibly route the whole pool on every unrouted proposal; DIK precedence over DRK would contain this without touching delegator finality
findings.description: Routes are one-shot per (round, d, p) and final. The DRK is hot and is used on every route. The identity spec accepts that a DRK thief "can at most route this round's un-routed proposals". That is still every unrouted proposal for the delegate's entire pool, and the pool's delegators cannot react, because owner decision 2 makes their delegation final. Decision 2 binds delegators, not routes, so a narrower route-finality rule is available.
findings.evidence: [doc] identity.md:57,123,129; integrated-design-v1.md:41,124-127.
findings.failure_scenario: Malware on the delegate's phone exfiltrates the session-unlocked DRK (identity.md:102). Minutes before vote end it submits a single `MsgDelegateRoute` covering all 50 proposals with the attacker's choices. The DIK holder rotates the DRK, but the routes stand. Thousands of delegators' weight is cast by the thief.
findings.proposed_fix: Let a DIK-signed route override a DRK route for the same (round, d, p) once, until vote_end_time. DIK beats DRK, and the DIK can be cold. Alternatively, record DRK routes as pending for delta minutes (finalized at min(t+delta, vote_end_time)) with a DIK cancel. Either keeps routes public and delegator DCs final.

findings.title: Coordinator suspension during a round turns committed, irrevocable delegations into forced abstention, a new coordinator lever over tally outcomes
findings.description: `MsgSetDelegateSuspension` blocks future routes immediately, and pools abstain where unrouted. Delegators cannot react, because DCs are final and the delegate index is hidden. Today the coordinator has no mid-round way to remove a set of voters' weight from specific proposals. The integrated doc says suspension "cannot void routes" but does not mention that it can prevent them.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:124-127,135; identity.md:118; chain.md:309-312.
findings.failure_scenario: A t-of-n coordinator quorum suspends a popular delegate an hour before vote end, before the delegate has routed, citing "impersonation". That delegate's entire pool abstains on every proposal; no route existed and none can be made.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the owner explicitly accept this power, or narrow it. Options: suspension affects only rounds created after it (wallets stop offering the delegate immediately); or a suspension inside an ACTIVE round takes effect only after a public delay that leaves the delegate time to route.

findings.title: `recovery_hint` reuses its ChaCha20-Poly1305 key and nonce whenever a broadcast DC is re-planned on the same input VAN with a different layout
findings.description: hint_key = H(ARK, van_nf) with nonce 0. `dc_seed` binds (d, w, layout), but the hint key does not. The client re-proves rejected batches and switches DCs to the single-share layout inside the last-moment window. A retry that crosses into that window re-encrypts a different plaintext (the layout byte) under the same key and nonce. Today the leak is only the layout bit, plus Poly1305 forgeability under that key; forgery is harmless because the sighash binds hints and recovery re-verifies the DC. It becomes a (d, w) leak if any path ever re-plans d or w after a broadcast, which `clear_proxy_allocation` currently prevents only by policy.
findings.evidence: [doc] client.md:215 (last-moment layout switch), client.md:232-249 (key, nonce, plaintext), client.md:506 (re-prove after a terminal rejection), client.md:512 (clear refused after a POST).
findings.failure_scenario: The first attempt (standard layout) is gossiped, then rejected at DeliverTx. The retry falls inside the last-moment window and uses layout 1. Both ciphertexts are public under the same (key, nonce), and their XOR reveals the layout change. Under any future re-plan rule it would also reveal d1^d2 and w1^w2.
findings.proposed_fix: Freeze (d, w, layout) per van_nf once a tx carrying the hint has been POSTed: keep the original layout on retry. Alternatively, put the layout into hint_key and try both layouts during recovery. Document the invariant next to the hint definition.

measurements:
Two throwaway Monte Carlo models are in scratchpad/review-privacy/.

(1) pool_inference.py → pool_inference.out (200 trials per cell). Public data is modelled as routes, per-option direct share counts and exact per-option totals. A bucket with zero direct shares that receives pools gives an exact equation, and a pool counts as exactly recoverable when e_d lies in the row space of those equations. Model assumptions: 85% per-proposal direct participation, 55/45 Yes/No, 2% direct Abstain, 85% route rate, 8% explicit delegate abstain.
- Abstain option counted, with unrouted and explicit-abstain pools added to it: P=15, 30 direct voters, 5 delegates → 4.05 of 5 pools (81%) exact. With 20 delegates → 2%, or 26% with a 1% minor option. P=5, 30 voters, 5 delegates → 27%. 200 voters → 0-10%. 1000 voters → 0.
- Sentinel semantics as designed: 0 exact pools with Yes/No-only proposals. With a 1%-direct minor option, 15% of pools are exact at P=15, 30 voters, 5 delegates, and about 0 at 200 or more voters.
- Conclusion: the Abstain-option mitigation increases exact disclosure in small and beta rounds.

(2) reveal_linking.py → reveal_linking.out (400 trials). A single-delegator pool in a 7-day round with a 6 h buffer, delays uniform in [0, min(100 h, deadline − t)) per zcash_voting share_policy. The anonymity set is the number of DC txs consistent with the pool's 16 reveal times. Medians are 4, 8, 29 and 112 at 0.1, 0.25, 1 and 4 DC txs per hour, and the pool is uniquely identified in 17%, 5%, 1% and 0% of cases. That is roughly 2/17 of the delay window, versus the full DC population the design assumes.
confirmations: delegate_index never appears in the DC tx or sighash; the recovery hint is a fixed 32 B AEAD; slot nullifiers are nk-keyed PRF outputs and unlinkable across txs (client.md §3.4, circuits.md §9).

The zero-nonce hint is safe in practice: plan-lock rules (clearing is refused once a POST is reserved, and re-proofs reuse dc_seed) mean the same hint_key only ever re-encrypts the same plaintext. The layout byte is the only exception.
The helper builds ZKP3 against the latest tree anchor (internal/helper/processor.go:766-778), so a reveal discloses nothing about leaf position beyond 'before the latest anchor'.

The routing hook decrypts only the final routed accumulators. rho is public but is meant to stop griefing, not to hide anything. Storing RoutingBase adds nothing beyond ciphertexts that are already public.
Proposal 0 is excluded from VoteSummary, which iterates round.Proposals (keeper_tally.go:197), and from ProposalTally (chain.md §5.3), so old explorers never show pools.

Whole-round route and pool endpoints exist (chain.md §5.3 RoundDelegateRoutes and DelegatePools). The directory is a whole-document download, lookup-only entries are k-anonymous by first byte of sha256(handle), and listed 64-px avatars come in one pack (identity.md:698, 719-721).
No X content goes on chain, in state or in tx bytes; only a salted subject_commit (identity.md:272-275).
Sentry already scrubs IP, non-basic headers and the /shares body (sentry.go:139-160), and helper spans omit vote_decision.
Vizor has no client analytics or crash SDK (vizor dossier §6), and the specs route avatars through NetworkHttpClient into Image.memory and Rust decoding.

Each share fans out to ceil(N/2) helpers, capped at 10 (share_policy/server_order.rs:51-53), so 'helpers' in the threat model means essentially every vote server. Each one learns d, the DC leaf and the client IP unless Tor is on, which is the same class as today's (p, o) leak for votes.
No new chain deadline and no intermediate decryption means there is no time-series differencing of tallies; pools are combined once, at the ACTIVE→TALLYING EndBlock.

findings.title: ARK keyed by the Orchard OVK lets every UFVK holder read the account's delegates and amounts, which are effectively its votes
findings.description: The account proxy recovery key is BLAKE2b keyed by the Orchard OVK. The OVK can be derived from the FVK, so anyone holding the UFVK can derive the ARK. They can then trial-decrypt every recovery hint in the public proxy-actions feed and recover (d, w, layout) for each of the account's DCs. Routes are public, so (d, w) shows exactly how the account's delegated weight voted on each proposal. Today vote secrets come only from the hotkey, so a UFVK holder can see that an account registered but not how it voted. This change is a regression in vote secrecy, not something covered by viewing-key semantics. Vizor gets nothing in return: its own recovery plan already says delegates and amounts are lost on reinstall, so it never uses the UFVK recovery path (R2).
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:172,176,236. [doc] specs/client.md §3.4 (ARK = BLAKE2b(key=ovk_orchard_external(FVK)); hint plaintext 0x01‖layout‖0x0000‖d‖w) and §3.10 R2 (scan the whole feed, about 1 µs per AEAD open). [doc] client.md §7: 'consistent with viewing-key semantics'. [code/doc] vizor docs/voting-participation.md:146: 'Lost voting hotkey secrets cannot be recreated from a wallet seed or Keystone UFVK' (today's votes are opaque to UFVK holders). [doc] specs/vizor.md:776 and :796 (C8): after a reinstall Vizor loses 'which delegates and amounts' and tells the user 'Vizor can't show it'. [inference] In Orchard the OVK is derived from the FVK via PRF_expand(rivk, ak, nk).
findings.failure_scenario: A Keystone user's UFVK sits in a watch-only wallet, with an accountant, or with an exchange or custodian. That party pulls `proxy-actions/{round}`, derives hint_key(ARK, van_nf) for each action and opens the AEADs. It learns that the account gave, for example, 4,000 ballots to delegate 17 and 2,400 to delegate 42. Joining that with the public routes, it knows how the account's ZEC voted on every proposal. The account never voted directly, and no secret except the UFVK was ever exposed.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the hotkey-derived ARK_hk the primary ARK for every account type. R1 recovery (DB lost, hotkey kept) is unchanged. For software accounts, optionally derive the ARK from seed-only material that is not in the FVK, such as a ZIP-32 registered path or PRF_expand of the Orchard spending key, so that a restore from seed gets R2 back. Offer recovery from the UFVK only as an explicit opt-in with copy explaining that viewing-key holders will see the account's delegations. Delete the 'consistent with viewing-key semantics' sentence, and keep hint_key = H(ARK, van_nf) otherwise unchanged. The cost is a few lines in the client and no change to circuits or chain.

verdict.reasoning: The finding is correct. The ARK is keyed by ovk_orchard_external(FVK). In Orchard the OVK is the second half of PRF_expand(rivk, 0x82||ak||nk), so anyone holding the UFVK can derive the ARK [inference]. They can then derive hint_key(ARK, van_nf) for every action in the public proxy-actions feed and open the 32-byte hints, recovering (d, w, layout). Routes are public, so (d, w) shows exactly how the account's delegated weight voted on each proposal. Today a UFVK holder learns only participation: Vizor derives governance nullifiers from the FVK, and vote secrets come from a random per-round hotkey that cannot be recreated from a UFVK. So this is a regression in vote secrecy towards viewing-key holders (watch-only wallets, accountants, explorers where users paste a UFVK), not something viewing-key semantics already cover. The only benefit is R2, and Vizor's own spec says it shows nothing after a reinstall, so Vizor never uses R2. ARK_hk is always available, because ZKP4 already needs the hotkey to sign under r_vpk, so swapping which key is primary costs nothing elsewhere. I lowered the severity from high to medium because the design states the consequence openly (integrated §5 and §8), so this is a mis-justified trade-off the owner can see. It is still a cheap change that must happen before the client is implemented.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:172 (ARK keyed by the Orchard OVK), :176 and :236 (UFVK holders see delegations). [doc] specs/client.md:220-238 (ARK and ARK_hk definitions, hint plaintext d‖w), :477-485 (R2 scans the feed, ~1 µs per open), :711 ('consistent with viewing-key semantics'). [doc] specs/vizor.md:776, :780 and :796 (after a reinstall Vizor loses 'which delegates and amounts'; 'Vizor can't show it'). R1 (DB lost, hotkey kept) is unchanged. Drop the UFVK-keyed R2 by default. If seed-restore recovery is wanted for software accounts, derive the ARK from spending-key material that is not in the FVK, under a new PRF_expand domain. Offer UFVK-keyed recovery only as an explicit opt-in, with copy saying that viewing-key holders will then see the account's delegations. Replace the client.md:711 sentence and integrated :176/:236 with 'Recovery hints are opaque to UFVK holders'. No change to circuits, chain or wire.

findings.title: Decision 4 cannot honestly be claimed as stated, and the proposed Abstain-option mitigation makes exact disclosure more likely
findings.description: The design names sole-contributor disclosure (a), turnout differencing (b) and EA decryption (c), but it misses four things. (1) Each option's direct share count is public, through VoteSummary BallotCount and the (p,o) attributes on reveal events. So a bucket with zero direct votes is visible to everyone, and every such bucket that receives pools gives an exact linear equation over the pools. Explorers will even show 'BallotCount 0, TotalValue X' for buckets that contain only pools. (2) An explicit Abstain option creates exactly these buckets, because direct voters seldom pick Abstain while delegates (and unrouted pools, if they are mapped there) do. The mitigation in the design therefore turns the approximate leak (b) into exact solutions, especially in small or [TEST] rounds. (3) A delegate can always disclose its own pool by routing to an option that has no direct shares, which it can check live. (4) Every share of a pool carries the public label d. So a t-of-n EA coalition gets the exact individual amount of a delegate's only delegator, and tight bounds when there are few delegators, without any help from the helpers. That contradicts spec T3 ('same protection as vote amounts') and Vizor copy C4 ('can't see ... how much you gave them ... same protection as a private vote'). Whenever a pool total becomes known and PoolShareCount equals 16, one delegator's amount becomes public.
findings.evidence: [code] vote-sdk x/vote/keeper/keeper_tally.go:197-209: VoteSummary exposes per-option BallotCount (direct reveals only) next to TotalValue. [code] msg_server_tally_decrypt.go:54-62: every reveal emits proposal_id and vote_decision. [doc] chain.md §6.2: ballot_count counts direct reveals only, and an empty bucket that receives a pool becomes the pool sum. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:221 and :232 (mitigation). [doc] spec_rollout.md T3 and T4. [doc] vizor.md C4 (copy deck, about line 791). [measured] review-privacy/pool_inference.py: with the Abstain option counted and 15 proposals, 30 direct voters and 5 delegates, 81% of pools are exactly solvable from public data. With sentinel semantics and only Yes/No options, 0% are.
findings.failure_scenario: A beta [TEST] round has 15 proposals, about 30 direct voters and an Abstain option on each proposal. Five delegates have pools, and a few of them abstain or leave proposals unrouted. Several Abstain buckets show BallotCount = 0. The published Abstain totals then form a solvable system, and anyone recovers about 4 of the 5 pool totals exactly. One of those delegates has PoolShareCount = 16, so that delegator's exact ZEC amount is public. If the immediate share (PRV-3) is kept, the amount is also tied to their transaction. Separately, a delegate who wants to prove its size to a vote buyer routes, at the last minute, to an option with zero direct shares.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Do not adopt a per-proposal Abstain option as a privacy mitigation. Keep the sentinel or unrouted semantics, where weight is not counted, so the residual leak is the approximate one (b). If an Abstain option is wanted for product reasons, adopt it only if the direct-vote UIs in both Zodl and Vizor present it, and never map unrouted pools into it. (2) Add an 'isolation check' to the delegate dashboard. Before the confirm sheet, compute from public BallotCount and routes whether this route would make any pool solvable, including another delegate's, and warn: 'No one has voted this option directly yet. If that stays true, your pool total will be public.' (3) In the delegator flow, show a notice when the chosen delegate's PoolShareCount is at most 16·k: 'You'd be one of very few people delegating to them; your amount may be inferable from final results.' (4) Fix the claims. Normative text for ZIP-PD and the book: "The protocol never decrypts an individual pool; only per-(proposal, option) totals are decrypted. Pool totals are therefore not published, but they are not guaranteed secret. (i) Any coalition holding at least t election-authority key shares can decrypt any pool and every pool share at any time. Because every share of a pool carries the public delegate index, this reveals individual delegation amounts for delegates with one delegator and narrow ranges for delegates with few. (ii) Per-option totals, routes and per-option direct share counts are public and exact. Anyone can compute a pool total whenever the published totals, minus contributions publicly known to be zero, determine it, for example when a delegate is the only router of an option that received no direct shares. A delegate can cause this deliberately. (iii) Pool totals can be estimated by comparing turnout across proposals when a delegate leaves proposals unrouted or abstains. (iv) The number of delegations each delegate receives is public. If a pool total becomes known and the pool has one delegator, that delegator's amount is known. Delegations do not have the same privacy as direct votes." Vizor C4: "Your delegate can't see who you are. Vizor never shows how much a delegate holds, and the voting chain never decrypts it. If very few people delegate to them, the total, and so your amount, can sometimes be worked out from the final results." Delegate DG-1 addition: "We don't publish how much was delegated to you, but it can sometimes be worked out from public results, especially if few people delegate to you or you vote for an option nobody else chose."

verdict.reasoning: The core mechanics hold. VoteSummary exposes per-(p,o) BallotCount from ShareCount, which counts direct reveals only, next to TotalValue. Every MsgRevealShare carries and emits (proposal_id, vote_decision). So a bucket with no direct shares is publicly identifiable, and its published total equals the sum of the pools routed into it. The design already lists the sole-contributor case as leak (a). The new and valid point is that the proposed mitigation, a per-proposal Abstain option, creates exactly these buckets. I re-ran the reviewer's model with the design's actual semantics: only explicit-abstain routes go to the Abstain option, and unrouted pools stay uncounted. With 15 proposals, 30 direct voters and 5 delegates, 42-44% of pools are exactly solvable, against 0% with sentinel abstain and Yes/No options only. With 200 direct voters it falls to 1-3%. The reviewer's 81% only holds if unrouted pools are also mapped into Abstain, which the design does not propose, so that number is overstated. The direction is right, but it matters mainly in small or [TEST] rounds. Point (4) is valid: every pool share carries the public label d, so for a delegate with one delegator, a ≥t EA coalition gets that DC's exact amount just by summing the 16 decrypted shares. That makes spec T3 ('same protection as vote amounts today') and Vizor C4 ('same protection as a private vote') overclaims. Point (3), a delegate disclosing its own pool, falls under the receipt-freeness the design already says it does not provide. I lowered the severity to medium: the Abstain option is still an open owner question (O5) and not yet adopted, the main leaks are already disclosed, and the fix is a decision plus copy and spec corrections.
verdict.evidence: [code] vote-sdk x/vote/keeper/keeper_tally.go:197-209 (BallotCount = GetShareCount next to TotalValue). [code] x/vote/keeper/msg_server_tally_decrypt.go:54-62 (IncrementShareCount; the event emits proposal_id and vote_decision). [doc] specs/chain.md:528 and :533 (an empty bucket becomes the pool sum; ballot_count counts direct reveals only). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:375-392 (T3 'same protection as vote amounts'; T4 mitigations include an Abstain option). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:229-232 and :261 (O5). [doc] specs/vizor.md:791 (C4). [measured] review-privacy-verify rerun of pool_inference with explicit-abstain-only mapping: P=15, 30 direct voters, 5 delegates → 0.42-0.44 exact; 200 direct voters → 0.02-0.03; sentinel → 0.00.
verdict.refined_fix: (1) Resolve O5 against adopting a per-proposal Abstain option as a privacy mitigation. Keep the sentinel abstain (recorded, not counted). If an Abstain option is wanted for product reasons, record that it creates pool-only buckets in small rounds. (2) Correct the claims. In T3, replace 'same protection as vote amounts' with: per-DC amounts are exposed to a ≥t EA coalition whenever a delegate has a single delegator, because every share carries d. In T4 and ZIP-PD, add that per-option direct share counts are public, so pool-only buckets are detectable, and that a delegate can deliberately isolate its pool. In Vizor C4, drop 'same protection as a private vote' and say amounts are not published but can sometimes be inferred when few people delegate to the same delegate. (3) Optional UX: an isolation warning on the delegate confirm sheet when the chosen option has zero direct shares, and a notice to delegators when the delegate's PoolShareCount ≤ 16. No circuit or chain change.

findings.title: The immediate share in proxy-only rounds is a DC share, which publicly ties the delegator's largest delegate to the DC transaction within seconds
findings.description: In a round where the user only delegates, the round's single immediate share (submit_at = 0) is designated as (highest bundle with a slot, slot 0, share 0). Slots are numbered by ballots descending, so slot 0 is the delegate receiving the most from that bundle. One or two blocks after the combined ZKP1+DC tx lands, a public reveal (0, d) appears. That links the tx, its registration and its k-DC count to its largest delegate. It also makes the remaining 15 reveals for d attributable, and combined with PoolShareCount it pins small pools to that tx. This contradicts integrated §8 ('unlinkable to the DC') and spec T2 ('hidden from A_pub'). The likely mode (Delegate everything, no own casts) always hits it.
findings.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:335-337 (proxy-only immediate share = slot 0, share 0, 'pending owner question 2'). [doc] client.md:169 (slot_index sorted by ballots descending). [doc] vizor.summary.md:46 (REQUIRES S6: immediate share covers DC shares) and vizor.md:207 (progress waits for the immediate share). [code] zcash_voting share_policy/initial_placement.rs:21-38 and docs/immediate-share-selection-plan.md (designated share gets submit_at = 0). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:221.
findings.failure_scenario: A user delegates everything: 60% to A, 30% to B, 10% to C. Shortly after the combined tx T, a reveal_share(0, A) is emitted. Anyone watching the chain now knows T's top allocation went to A. If A has only this delegator, the later 15 reveals and any disclosure of A's pool total (PRV-2) become T's exact amount. The EA also learns one share plaintext of T's DC.
findings.proposed_fix: Never designate a DC share as the immediate share. In proxy-only rounds there should be no immediate share. Advance the progress screen on DC inclusion plus durable helper acceptance of the DC shares (the existing helper quorum confirmation), and track reveals in the background. If a reveal-liveness probe is truly required, use a normally delayed share and poll its status. Record owner question 2 as resolved this way, and correct integrated §8.

verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is real. In a proxy-only round the client spec designates (highest bundle with a slot, slot 0, share 0) as the immediate share with submit_at = 0. Its reveal (0, d) lands right after the proxy tx and publicly links that anonymous tx to one delegate. That contradicts integrated §8 ('unlinkable to the DC') and T2 ('hidden from A_pub'). However, this is exact parity with what today's vote path already accepts. MsgCastVote carries proposal_id in clear, and the vote immediate share (share 0 of the lowest voted proposal in the lowest-value bundle, submit_at = 0) reveals (p, o) right after the cast, which links that anonymous tx to its choice. The delegator's identity stays hidden in both cases. The client spec also already flags the issue (client.md:337 and :705, 'owner question 2'). The real defect is that the integrated doc dropped that caveat. Smaller corrections: slot 0 is the largest delegate within the lowest-value bundle that has a slot, not necessarily the user's largest delegate overall, and share 0 holds a shuffled denomination, not w.
verdict.evidence: [code] zcash_voting share_policy/initial_placement.rs:30-39 (immediate key = highest bundle, lowest voted proposal, share 0). [doc] zcash_voting docs/immediate-share-selection-plan.md:5-27 (designated share gets submit_at = 0). [code] vote-sdk proto tx.proto:76-88 (MsgCastVote.proposal_id is public). [code] internal/helper/store.go:466-506 (submit_at = 0 is scheduled immediately). [doc] specs/client.md:169, :335-337 and :705 (already says 'unlinkable ... except through the immediate share (owner question 2)'). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:221. [doc] specs/vizor.md:207 and :502 (progress waits for the immediate share).
verdict.refined_fix: Resolve owner question 2 explicitly. The preferred option, since it is better than today's vote path at little cost: in proxy-only rounds, designate no immediate share, and let Vizor's PD-6 'Sending shares to helpers' step complete on durable helper acceptance of all DC shares rather than on an on-chain reveal. Keep the existing rule when the round has a vote. If the owner keeps a DC immediate share, amend integrated §8:221 and T2 to say that one delegate choice per proxy-only registration is linkable to its tx, the same as the vote immediate share.

findings.title: Small pools and last-moment DCs are linkable from reveal timing, and three specs give conflicting late-delegation cutoffs
findings.description: For votes, the random delays work because one label (p,o) is shared by many VCs. For a delegate with one or a few delegators, the public label d groups all 16 reveals of a DC. The only candidate DC txs are then those whose delay window covers the earliest and latest of those reveals, an interval about 2W/17 wide. Inside the last-moment buffer (40% of the round, capped at 6 h), every share gets submit_at = 0. In addition, client spec §3.3 switches DCs to the single-share layout there. That publicly links d to the tx, gives the EA the exact w, and makes PoolShareCount mod 16 count the late DCs. The rules disagree: Vizor allows delegating until end − 10 min, the client uses the single-share layout in the last-moment window, and the integrated doc says delegation is blocked inside the buffer with a 30-min hard cutoff.

findings.title: Per-key chain queries reveal which delegates were chosen, and random decoys are defeated by intersection
findings.description: The integrated design and the client and Vizor specs prove delegate records, routes and DC share nullifiers by point lookups. The keys contain d, or nullifiers whose public reveal events contain d. Lookups run at preview, at commit and immediately before proving, then again on the status screen. Each batch re-draws 3 random decoys, so intersecting two or three batches isolates the real delegates. The pre-proving batch comes from the same IP seconds before the DC tx POST. This conflicts with the identity spec ('never query per index as a delegator') and reverses an existing design choice: helper share-status exists to avoid exposing a public chain nullifier query to wallets. Tor is off by default. Vote servers also run the helper on the same router, so they already see d in cleartext share payloads. That means the decoys protect only against third-party RPCs, CDNs and logs, and should not be described as protection.

To verify without per-key proofs, add single-key digests: a registry digest updated on each registry op, a per-round route-set hash chain, and a per-round pool-reveal-nullifier hash chain. The client downloads the paged list, recomputes the digest and checks one IAVL proof. The cost is one hash per op. If decoys stay, make them sticky per (wallet, round), popularity-matched and at least 8. Keep share confirmation on helper share-status, and drop chain NullifierStatus from the wallet path. At the review step, prompt the user to turn Tor on for the delegation flow, since Vizor already ships arti.

verdict.reasoning: The spec conflict and the decoy weakness are real. Identity §5.5 says 'never query per index as a delegator'. Client §5.3 fetches /delegates/{d} at preview, at commit and before proving. Vizor §7.9 IAVL-proves per-delegate keys with 3 freshly drawn random decoys per batch, which intersection across batches defeats. But the marginal privacy loss is small. Each DC share goes to ceil(N/2) helpers, so every helper operator sees d for essentially every DC, together with the client IP, at submission. That is accepted in T2 (not hidden from A_help). The RPC Vizor proves against is vote-rpc-primary.valargroup.org, run by Valar, which also runs helpers. So the per-key queries mostly tell an operator what its helpers already learn seconds later. The new exposure is limited to third-party infrastructure in front of the RPC (TLS terminators, CDN, logs) and to delegates previewed but never chosen. The existing participation reader already accepts the same non-PIR per-key leak. The reviewer's chain-digest proposal is heavier than this warrants.

findings.title: Helper and REST telemetry sends Sentry the data that links every reveal, pool reveals included, to its commitment leaf
findings.description: For each enqueued share, the helper attaches proposal_id, tree_position and submit_at to a Sentry span. The POST /shares transaction is sampled at 1.0 in production, and process_share at 0.1. Matching submit_at, or the processing time, with the public reveal event, which carries (0, d), links each DC leaf and tx to its delegate. That defeats the random delays for anyone with access to the Sentry project, and for Sentry itself, without being a helper operator. The REST tracing names transactions by raw path, because gorilla/mux does not set r.Pattern. So the new routes would also send 'GET /shielded-vote/v1/delegates/17' and nullifier paths to Sentry. vote_decision is already omitted and IPs are scrubbed, but the remaining fields are enough to reconstruct the link.

Name HTTP transactions by route template (mux.CurrentRoute(r).GetPathTemplate()) in a wrapper. Set the sample rate to 0 for delegate, nullifier and share-status routes. Add a test that fails if span data contains those keys.

verdict.reasoning: The code matches the finding. The helper.enqueue span (child of the sentryhttp 'POST /shielded-vote/v1/shares' transaction, sampled at 1.0 in production) and the helper.process_share transaction (sampled at 0.1) carry proposal_id, tree_position and submit_at. BeforeSendTransaction only clears the IP, non-basic headers and the /shares request body; span data is untouched. gorilla/mux leaves r.Pattern empty, so sentryhttp names transactions by raw URL path, which the sampler's prefix match on share-status paths confirms. Joining submit_at or the processing time with the public reveal event (p, o) links a commitment leaf, and so its tx, to its decision; for DCs that would be d. I lowered the severity because this is pre-existing for votes and not created by the delegation design. The Sentry project only receives Valar's own fleet, whose helpers already hold (tree_position, vote_decision) in their stores. The extra exposure is to Sentry as a subprocessor and to staff with Sentry access. It is a cheap hygiene fix that should land with the helper's proposal-0 branch.

findings.title: Vote servers can link a delegate's private votes to their public identity
findings.description: The integrated design mentions the same-IP linkage only in passing, and Vizor ships it as a non-enforced 'timing hint'. In practice the same svoted server receives the delegate's route POSTs, signed by the DRK and publicly attributable to their X identity, and the delegate's own helper share POSTs, which carry the vote decision in cleartext. Tor is off by default, and DG-9 places 'Vote publicly' and 'Your private vote' side by side, which invites doing both in one session. Restore scans of /delegates/by-key from the same IP that runs the participation reader add more linkage. The copy 'Your private votes stay private' overclaims.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:238. [doc] vizor.md:316, :380-387 and :405. [code] app/app.go:386-392 (one router for tx and helper). [code] internal/helper/types.go:117-127 (SharePayload.VoteDecision in cleartext). [code] network_privacy_provider.dart:79. [doc] client.md:596 and identity.md:92 (by-key scans).

The vote server sees the route tx and 16 or more share payloads with her decisions from the same IP within minutes. It learns her private votes, her registration and her bundle count, even if she votes against her public routes.
findings.proposed_fix: In delegate mode, require Tor for route submission and for the delegate account's own vote and share traffic, or use separate Tor circuits for each, or at least make Tor default-on with a blocking prompt. Submit routes to a different vote server than the one carrying the account's shares, and add a random delay. Move the private-vote CTA out of DG-9. Change the copy to: 'Your private votes are hidden from the public. Vote servers can link them to you unless Tor is on.' After private-vote V2, the residual leak is participation linkage only.

verdict.reasoning: Valid. A delegate's MsgDelegateRoute is DRK-signed and publicly bound to their X identity, and it is POSTed to a vote server. Their own private-vote shares, with vote_decision in cleartext, go to ceil(N/2) helpers, which almost certainly include that operator. Tor is off by default. So any helper operator links IP to public identity to private votes, deterministically, which is worse than for an ordinary voter, whose IP is not otherwise tied to a public identity. The design notes this in one line (§8:238), but Vizor ships only an unenforced 'timing hint', and DG-1's 'Your private votes stay private' plus DG-9's side-by-side columns overclaim and invite doing both in one session. The reviewer's suggestion to submit routes to a different vote server adds little, because shares already go to half of all helpers, so I dropped it. The residual after private-vote V2 is participation linkage, as the reviewer says.

[doc] specs/vizor.md:316 ('Your private votes stay private'), :385-387 (DG-9 side by side, 'Only you can see this'), :405 (timing hint, no enforcement). [code] vote-sdk internal/helper/types.go:117-127 (SharePayload.VoteDecision in clear). [code] app/app.go:386-392 (tx, query and helper routes on one svoted router). Replace 'Your private votes stay private' with 'Your private votes are hidden from the public. Vote servers can link them to you unless Tor is on.' findings.title: X compliance gaps, and an overstated crypto-shredding claim about unlinking identities
findings.description: (1) The registry doc publishes subject.id and salt to every wallet and to two mirrors. Anyone who cached any version can recompute subject_commit forever, so shredding the salt does not make on-chain routes unlinkable. Delegates must be told that attribution is permanent. (2) The profiles doc expiry is 30 h, but X requires deletion within 24 h of deletion on X or a request, so offline or failed-refresh wallets can display deleted content too long. (3) Documents and avatar packs are content-addressed with immutable caching, and nothing deletes superseded registry, profiles or pack objects or purges the pull-through mirror. (4) X's restricted-use policy says 'Never derive or infer, or store derived or inferred, information about a X user's ... Political affiliation or beliefs'. The X-keyed registry doc stores voting 'activity', and the deeplink page advertises a 'public voting record'. Governance votes keyed by X user id need legal review. Off-X matching also needs express opt-in consent, yet the marker line is deliberately brand-neutral and contains no consent text. X's new ToS takes effect 2026-10-09.

[doc] identity.md:603-608, :718 and :720 (content-addressed objects, max-age 1y immutable). [doc] identity.md:623 ('activity'). [doc] vizor.md:737. [doc] dossiers/identity_research.md:196-199. [doc] fetched 2026-10-05 docs.x.com/developer-terms/more-on-restricted-use-cases (political affiliation restriction; express opt-in for off-X matching) and docs.x.com/developer-terms/policy (24 h).
findings.failure_scenario: A delegate deletes their X account. Valar purges within 6 h, but every archived registry doc still maps index 17 to X id 1234567890, so their on-chain routes stay attributed to them permanently. A wallet that was offline still shows the old profile 28 h later. registry/<old-sha>.json.gz is still served by the CDN. An X compliance review flags a public dataset of X users' governance positions keyed by user id.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the shredding claim and add to DG-1: 'Your public votes stay linked to your X account permanently, even if you delete your post or account.' Set the profiles doc expires_at to at most issued + 24 h minus the purge SLA. Delete superseded registry, profiles and pack objects (keep only current plus a short overlap) and purge both the CDN and the functions.vizor.cash mirror. Remove 'activity' from the X-keyed document and have wallets compute it from chain routes. Add explicit consent text to the DIK-signed statement shown at onboarding and retain it as the consent record. Get legal sign-off against the 2026-10-09 terms before launch.

verdict.reasoning: Items (1) to (3) are valid spec gaps. (1) Identity §3.1 claims that deleting the salt makes the on-chain subject_commit unlinkable, but the public registry doc publishes subject.id and salt to every wallet and both mirrors, so anyone who cached any version can recompute the commit forever. The claim is false, and delegates should be told that attribution is permanent. (2) The profiles doc expires up to 30 h after issue, while the deletion duty is 24 h. A wallet whose refresh fails can keep showing purged data past 24 h. Whether device caches fall under the duty is a legal question, but an expiry of 24 h minus the purge SLA is cheap. (3) The purge rewrites 'the next registry doc' and purges avatars, but nothing deletes superseded registry/profiles/<sha> objects or purges the functions.vizor.cash pull-through mirror. That contradicts the spec's own 'nothing X-derived in immutable stores' intent. (4) is weak. X's off-X matching rule (fetched today) exempts associations based on 'information provided directly to you by the user', which covers the delegate's own marker post and DIK-signed binding. The 'political affiliation' restriction concerns deriving or inferring that from X data, whereas routes are the delegate's own explicit public on-chain actions and 'activity' holds only routed counts. Identity §5.2 already flags the 2026-10-09 terms for legal review. Explicit consent text is prudent, not required.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/identity.md:273-275 (crypto-shredding claim) vs :583 and :619-625 (registry doc carries subject.id and salt, public and cross-wallet). [doc] identity.md:588-593 (30 h expiry, 24 h duty, purge covers 'the next registry doc' and avatars only). [doc] identity.md:607-610 and :685 (content-addressed registry/profiles paths, pull-through mirror) and :718 (immutable caching, max-age 1 y). [doc] identity.md:589 (legal review already flagged). [doc] fetched docs.x.com/developer-terms/more-on-restricted-use-cases: opt-in is required for off-X matching, except for 'Information provided directly to you by the user' and public profile data; the political-affiliation rule is 'Never derive or infer'.
verdict.refined_fix: Delete the crypto-shredding sentence in identity §3.1 and add to DG-1: 'Your public votes stay linked to your X account permanently, even if you later delete your post or account.' Set the profiles doc expires_at ≤ issued + (24 h − purge SLA). Add a retention rule: after a purge, delete superseded registry and profiles objects and packs that contain the purged subject (keeping current plus a short overlap), and purge both the CDN and the functions.vizor.cash mirror. Optionally add one consent line to the DIK-signed binding statement and keep it as the consent record. Keep the existing legal-review gate. Removing 'activity' from the registry doc is optional.

findings.title: Smaller interest and amount leaks: DC order sorted by size, deep-link path, avatar fallback
findings.description: (1) Slots are numbered by ballots descending, and leaves are appended in action order [inference: actions follow slot order]. Each share fans out to ceil(N/2) helpers, so every helper sees every DC leaf of the tx with its d, and learns the ranking of the user's allocations. That contradicts 'helpers do not learn amounts'. (2) Deep links put the index in the path (/d/<index>), so a desktop or browser open logs IP plus index at the deeplink host and CDN. (3) The identity spec puts the listed 64-px pack at about 5 MB for 10k delegates, but Vizor uses the pack only when it is at most 4 MB and otherwise fetches by hash in visible order. 256-px profile avatars are also fetched by hash. Both reveal browsing and selection to the directory CDN.

Always use packs: shard the listed pack by index range rather than falling back to per-hash fetches, and serve 256-px images only through prefix-shard packs, or upscale the 64-px image for the header.

measurements:
Queue model in scratchpad/review-liveness/helper_load_sim.py and scale_sweep.py, pure Python, about 17 s per run.

Assumptions:
- Round of 7 days; last-moment window L = min(40% of the round, 6 h) = 6 h.
- Standard commitments emit 16 shares with submit_at uniform in [t, min(t + 100 h, T - L)]. Commitments made inside the window emit 1 immediate share.
- One global FIFO ordered by eligible time. Service rate mu = 10 operators x 2 workers x 0.58 / dup.
- A share is lost if it completes after T - 5 min.
- Arrival profiles: 'uniform' over the round, or 'deadline' (50% before T-24h, 35% in [T-24h, T-6h], 15% in [T-6h, T-10min]).
- Direct-vote baseline: 5k voters x 10 proposals.

Results as lost weight, DC / direct-vote (VC):

| Scenario | dup | Uniform | Deadline-heavy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Votes only | 1 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (backlog 0.5 h at T-6h) |
| Votes only | 2 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (backlog 4.6 h at T-6h) |
| 5k delegators x 3 (L2-like) | 1 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| 5k delegators x 3 (L2-like) | 2 | 0 / 0 | 20.4% / 19.5% |
| 10k x 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (backlog 2.8 h at T-6h) |
| 10k x 3 | 2 | 0 / 0 | 26.5% / 26.1% |
| 20k x 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 | 15.5% / 14.5% |
| 20k x 3 | 2 | 4.7% / 4.8% | 34.4% / 33.9% |
| 50k x 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 (backlog 5.2 h at T-6h) | 31.9% / 30.6% |
| 50k x 3 | 2 | 25.2% / 24.0% | 45.8% / 44.5% |
| 50k x 3 | 5 | 62.0% / 60.8% | 66.1% / 65.6% |

Mitigation runs at 50k x 3, dup = 1:
- 4 workers per operator (23.2/s): 0 loss; deadline backlog 4.7 h.
- 6 workers per operator (34.8/s): 0 loss; deadline backlog 1.6 h.

Arithmetic for 50k x 3 (one bundle each, 150k DCs; up to 200k at D+B-1 with 2 bundles):
- Reveals: 2.4M (3.2M at 200k DCs).
- Saturated chain reveal capacity (256 per 1.2 s block, about 213/s): 3.1 h. Not binding; about 18x helper capacity.
- Helper fleet proving: 57 h for DC shares alone (74 h including the direct votes) at 11.6/s with perfect dedupe.
- Each helper holds about 50% of all shares (target 5 of 10). Proving everything it holds would take about 370 h per helper, so capacity depends entirely on commit-based dedupe.
- Chain DC txs: about 50k. ZKP4 verify about 1.9 ms x 2 (CheckTx + DeliverTx), about 5 CPU-min in total.
- Tree leaves: about 250k per round, against a 16.7M capacity.
- EndBlock routing: 1k delegates x 50 routes about 0.5 s, 10k x 50 about 1.4 s (chain spec, M3 Ultra).

Caveats: the 0.58/s figure is a staging measurement. ZKP3 proves in about 26 ms on desktop, so the helper pipeline, not proving, appears to be the bound. The duplicate-proof factor is unmeasured and should be measured.
confirmations: Hardware delegators: Vizor collects device signatures for every pending bundle before any submission (vizor lib/src/providers/voting/voting_session_provider.dart:731-739). The Keystone/Ledger path adds no per-bundle broadcast gap. Signed ZKP1s are independent of DC plans and survive a re-plan.
Helper enqueue idempotency ignores submit_at (internal/helper/store.go:2163-2186). R2 redelivery of rebuilt DC shares with a new submit_at is accepted as a duplicate, not a conflict.

dc_seed binds (van_nf, d, w, layout) (specs/client.md:232-237), so a crash before broadcast re-proves without El Gamal nonce reuse. The hint carries the layout, so recovery can re-derive whichever layout actually landed.

The chain accepts proposal-0 reveals regardless of delegate status (chain spec and identity.md:439). Freezes, suspensions and revocations after a DC was made do not strand its already-delivered shares; the pool simply abstains where unrouted.
The C14 limit of 16 DC slots per registration chain does not constrain the 10-delegate UX cap or D+B-1 splits (at most 10 slots per bundle).
The 256-reveals-per-block cap is not the binding constraint at realistic fleet sizes; helper proving is (see measurements).
Tree capacity (2^24 leaves per round) and EndBlock routing cost are comfortable at 50k delegators.
The chain spec's weight-loss enumeration (chain.md:591-599) is sound, but it depends on the stored DC cutoff that the integrated design dropped (see LIV-4).
Each share is sent to ceil(N/2) helpers (server_order.rs:51-53), so a single lagging or down helper does not lose a share. The risk is fleet-wide backlog, not single-helper failure.

findings.title: Helper fleet, not the chain, caps proxy delegation at scale, and an overload also drops Zodl's direct votes
findings.description: Each DC adds 16 helper ZKP3 proofs. They join the same per-round FIFO as vote shares, ordered by effective submit_at with no class priority. The plan's capacity argument (chain.md:721: delegating 1 DC instead of voting P proposals 'reduces helper load by a factor of P') only holds when delegators would otherwise have voted directly. The feature targets passive holders, so most DCs are added load. Fleet capacity at the default config is 10 operators x 2 workers x 0.58 = 11.6 proofs/s, and that assumes no fleet-wide duplicate proving. Duplicates are likely because each share is enqueued at ceil(N/2) = 5 helpers. All five hold it at the same submit_at, and dedupe only skips a share whose reveal is already committed. The 256-per-block reveal cap (about 213/s) is roughly 18x above helper capacity and is not the bottleneck. When the backlog passes the last-moment window, the shares lost belong to both DCs and direct votes, including Zodl's. The rollout load matrix (L1-L3: 5k voters, 5k delegators x 2.5 DCs, uniform) is too small to catch this.

[inference] Throughput is therefore pipeline-bound, not proof-bound.
findings.failure_scenario: 7-day round. 50k delegators x 3 delegates = 150k DCs = 2.4M reveals, plus 5k direct voters x 10 proposals (0.8M), at 11.6 proofs/s. Uniform arrivals: no loss, but a 5.2 h backlog at T-6h, which fails the rollout's own 30%-headroom criterion. Deadline-heavy arrivals (35% in the last 24 h before the 6 h window, 15% inside it): 31.9% of DC weight and 30.6% of direct-vote weight miss vote_end_time even with perfect dedupe. At a 2x duplicate-proof factor, 10k delegators x 3 already loses about 26%. The losses are silent partial counts in Pool[d] and in Zodl voters' accumulators.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Add a capacity SLO and a release gate. Extend the load matrix to 20k and 50k delegators with deadline-heavy arrivals, and measure proofs per unique reveal (the duplicate factor). (2) Remove duplicate proving: give each share a deterministic primary helper, ranked by H(share_nf || helper_id). Secondaries prove only after k blocks with no reveal. (3) Find out what bounds the 1.7 s/share pipeline, given the 26 ms prove, and raise workers per helper. 4 workers per operator brings the 50k deadline case to 0 loss at perfect dedupe in the model. (4) Add an admission signal: the client reads the helper's public per-round QueueSummary and warns, or refuses new standard-layout DCs, when the projected backlog exceeds the time left before the window. Use a per-round min_ballots_per_delegate to cap dust DCs. (5) Correct the 'reduces load' claim in chain.md:721 and in the ZIP.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanics are right. DC shares go into the same per-round helper FIFO as vote shares. Each share goes to ceil(N/2) helpers. Pre-proof dedupe checks only committed nullifiers, so duplicate proving happens. The plan's 'reduces helper load by a factor of P' is a substitution argument that fails for delegators who would not otherwise vote. The load matrix (L2/L3: 5k delegators, voters arriving uniformly) never tests delegators outnumbering direct voters, deadline-heavy arrivals, or proofs per unique reveal. Z12 checks only the 256/block chain cap, not helper contention for Zodl shares.

'High / likely production failure' does not hold up:
(a) The bottleneck and the duplicate proving are pre-existing helper properties, not something proxy delegation introduces. Per user, delegation is cheaper than voting: 3 DCs = 48 reveals, versus 160 (10 proposals) or 592 (37 proposals) for one direct voter.
(b) I re-ran the reviewer's own model with direct votes only. It predicts heavy loss for today's system at plausible scales: 2k voters x 37 proposals, deadline-heavy arrivals, dup=2 gives 21% VC loss; 5k x 37 at dup=1 gives 29%. So either the 0.58/s and duplicate inputs are pessimistic, or the existing fleet is already near its limit. In both cases the 50k-delegator scenario is a stress assumption, not a likely outcome.

What is real: the plan has no helper-capacity budget for additive delegators, and its rollout gate would not catch a regression that delays Zodl reveals. That needs fixing in the rollout plan before activation.

(2) Extend §5.6 with an additive-delegator case (delegators 2-4x direct voters), deadline-heavy arrival profiles for both populations, and a wide-ballot (37-proposal) baseline. On the ten-helper lab, measure proofs per unique reveal and per-share pipeline time. (3) Add a release gate: Zodl direct-vote reveal loss and latency in the mixed scenario must not regress against the matching direct-only baseline. Raise helper workers or capacity to the measured headroom before enabling proxy delegation on production rounds. A deterministic primary-helper dedupe and a client admission signal are optional, pre-existing helper improvements; track them separately, not as prerequisites.

findings.title: The 'safe to leave' point is wrong for delegators, and Vizor does not wire R2 share redelivery
findings.description: A DC consumes the VAN when it is included. Its weight reaches Pool[d] only if its shares reach helpers. Vizor ends the job when the round's immediate share is confirmed on chain (revealed), not when the DC shares have been handed to helpers. (1) Under a helper backlog, the immediate share waits behind the FIFO for hours (LIV-1), so the progress screen hangs and users leave. (2) In a proxy-only round with no immediate DC share (client open question 2, still undecided), hasConfirmedImmediateShare returns true when the key is null. The job can then report COMPLETE right after inclusion, before initial delivery has finished. (3) Mobile Dart work is foreground-only, Vizor has no voting background task, and no wakelock exists anywhere in lib/. Screen auto-lock therefore pauses delivery. (4) The integrated design (section 5) relies on R1/R2 to rebuild and redeliver DC shares after DB loss. The Vizor spec does not implement them and its copy claims the opposite.
findings.evidence: [doc] specs/vizor.md:207 'Sending shares to helpers: until the immediate share is confirmed'; vizor.md:502,516 deliveringShares -> COMPLETE on immediate share confirmed; [code] vizor-wallet lib/src/features/voting/voting_resume_plan.dart:11-19 (returns true when immediateShareKey == null); [code] zcash_voting docs/migrating-to-v5.md:261-264 (foreground confirms only the immediate share; the rest needs a host background task); [code] lib/src/core/layout/app_process_work_policy.dart:4-17 (mobile foreground-only); [code] grep shows no wakelock in vizor lib/; [doc] vizor.md:776,780,796 (C8: 'your delegation still counts, but Vizor can't show it'; reinstall row says shares were 'handed to helpers at submission'); [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:176 and specs/client.md:470-483 (R2 rebuild plus redeliver).
findings.failure_scenario: A user on a phone taps 'Delegate 37.5 ZEC'. The combined ZKP1+DC tx is included. The phone screen locks, or the app crashes, while the 48 DC share POSTs are still in flight. The user believes delegation is done, and it is final, so they never reopen Vizor, or they reinstall later. None of the DC shares reach helpers. The VAN is spent, so Pool[d] never gets the weight, and Vizor's copy told the user it 'still counts'.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the leave-safe point as: every DC share has definite acceptance from target_count helpers (the delivery result, not chain confirmation). Show it as 'Handed off'. Keep immediate-share confirmation as a separate, non-blocking indicator. Hold a wakelock from proving through delivery. Implement R2 in Vizor: on startup and on poll open, for any proxy-enabled ACTIVE round where the participation reader finds spent governance nullifiers but there is no local proxy state, run the gov-nullifier lookup, decrypt the hint, rebuild the DC and redeliver its shares (helper enqueue is idempotent across submit_at). Replace C8 with accurate copy.

verdict.reasoning:
Most sub-claims do not show weight loss specific to proxy delegation.
(1) The SDK's immediate-share gate waits only for the designated share's definite helper acceptance, not chain confirmation, before delivering the other shares. Vizor awaits castVotes, which runs initial delivery, before it checks completion. A backlog therefore delays the 'Done' screen but does not hold back DC share handoff.
(2) With a null immediate key, the job still completes only after the awaited SDK run, which includes initial delivery. The client spec also already designates a proxy-only immediate share (pending OQ2, recommendation yes). 'COMPLETE right after inclusion, before delivery' is not supported.
(3) Foreground-only mobile work and the lack of a wakelock are identical for direct votes today. A restart with the DB intact resumes delivery through the share-tracking restorer, so no wakelock is needed to avoid loss.

What remains real:
- Vizor's reinstall row and copy C8 claim the delegation 'still counts, because shares were handed to helpers at submission'. That holds only if initial delivery completed.
- The Vizor spec never wires the client's R1/R2 rebuild-and-redeliver, which integrated-design §5 relies on.
- Vizor's COMPLETE gate silently depends on OQ2 staying 'yes'.
These are narrow windows (DB loss between DC inclusion and delivery) and doc inconsistencies, so low.
