verdict.refined_fix:
1. Drop `unfreeze` and keep the identity-spec semantics. If unfreeze must stay, make it DIK-only and have it increment key_epoch, counted toward max_key_changes. That kills every earlier freeze, unfreeze and route signature with no new field and bounds toggling to 64.
2. In Prepare/ProcessProposal, dedupe registry ops by delegate_index (at most one per delegate per block), mirroring the share-nullifier dedupe. This stops one delegate from filling the cap with duplicate-signature copies. Reserved capacity per op type is unnecessary because FIFO ordering already bounds the delay.
3. Bind ctx.ChainID() into every registry and route digest, as chain.md D3-D7 and spec_rollout:245 already do.
4. Add a test that rebroadcasts a committed registry tx after cache eviction and expects rejection.

findings.title: The genesis and chain-reset contract has not been updated for the integrated design: slot nullifiers fail validation and PoolShareCount is never exported
findings.description: The integrated design adds three things the chain spec's genesis section (written for a different message and key set) does not cover: dc_slot_nf in a new nullifier set 0x03, a separate PoolShareCount instead of ShareCount, and a registry family (DIK, DRK, used attestation ids, pending changes) with a different prefix layout. ExportGenesis exports every nullifier type it finds under 0x01, but ValidateGenesisState rejects any nullifier_type > 2. After the first proxy round, the export-then-reset path therefore fails `svoted genesis validate`. If validation is simply relaxed, PoolShareCount and any recovery-feed index are silently dropped unless they are added to GenesisState. Height-keyed cursors (`updated_since_height`, `from_height`) also go stale on a reset unless the new genesis carries `initial_height` past the old chain height.

findings.proposed_fix: Write one normative GenesisState section for ZIP-PD/ZIP-DR covering nullifier types 0-3, PoolShareCount, every 0x1A registry subkey (including used attestation ids and pending changes), routes, routing bases, params, NextDelegateIndex and any recovery index. The genesis contract is stale against the integrated design. ValidateGenesis rejects nullifier_type > 2, while the exporter emits every type byte under 0x01. chain.md §5.2 assumes pool counts ride in share_counts and has no slot nullifiers, DRK, attestation ids or 0x1A sub-keys. The operational impact is overstated. Chain resets in this project are fresh-genesis wipes (init.sh), not export and re-import, and upgrades run in place, so the export-validate path is not the reset path. The claim that slot nullifiers are lost is also wrong. The exporter already emits type 3 and NullifierKey accepts any type byte, so relaxing the validator imports them correctly; only PoolShareCount and the registry need new fields. Fresh-genesis resets restart heights and wipe the registry anyway, so a runbook rule on `initial_height` would not apply. Wallets just need to scope height cursors by chain ID. This is a spec-completeness item, so low.

findings.title: The recovery feed and the height-incremental queries have no defined backing store; an event-backed feed is incomplete on validators restored from snapshots
findings.description: The integrated design adds `proxy-actions/{round}?from_height` (the R1/R2 recovery feed, including tx_hash and recovery_hint), `delegates?updated_since_height` and an "incremental" `delegate-routes/{round}`. Neither the chain spec nor the integrated design defines state or indexes behind them: the chain spec has only start_index paging and no recovery hint at all. There are three ways to serve them, and the first two fail. (1) From events through the Comet tx index: snapshot nodes run `indexer = "null"` and validators join by restoring those snapshots, so most vote servers lack history before their restore, and a reset erases it everywhere. Hints authenticate themselves but not completeness, so an incomplete answer looks valid. (2) By full scans over registry or route state per request: the REST API is unauthenticated and fee-less, so cheap requests can force O(registry) or O(routes) work. (3) KV secondary indexes: these work but must be added to the state-growth estimate and to genesis.

The integrated design adds an IAVL-provable `nullifier/{round}/{type}/{nf}` query, so an R1 wallet can detect that VAN_i was spent without a matching feed entry. findings.title: Mainnet [TEST]-round beta is unresolved for Zodl and is tied to a global, irreversible round-creation flag
findings.description: The integrated design says "Beta runs on [TEST] rounds", and the Vizor spec plans a public beta on mainnet [TEST] rounds. Vizor's [TEST] filter applies only to authenticated rounds, so a public beta round must be signed into the prod dynamic config. Zodl (local checkout a893c64a) lists every authenticated chain round with no [TEST] filtering; endorsement is only an icon plus an "unverified poll" sheet, so Zodl users will see and can enter the test polls. Leaving the round unsigned is also not safe enough. Zodl parses every round returned by `/rounds`, which never deletes rounds, before authenticating it, and that parse sits outside the per-round catch. One test round that fails Zodl's validateProposals (this checkout allows only 1-15 proposals and contiguous 0-indexed options) therefore makes fetchAllRounds throw and blanks Zodl's whole poll list permanently. Separately, the proxy enable bit is snapshotted from the global `enable_for_new_rounds` when a threshold-approved MsgCreateVotingSession executes, and it is immutable afterwards. Toggling the flag for beta rounds can turn the next production round into a proxy round, or leave it a plain one, depending on when the last approval lands. Any ACTIVE [TEST] round also blocks the between-rounds upgrade window.

findings.failure_scenario: (a) A mainnet [TEST] proxy round with 20 or 50 proposals, used to exercise routing at scale, is created and left unsigned. Every Zodl build with this parse-before-auth loop now shows "couldn't load polls" for all rounds, because rounds are never pruned. (b) A signed [TEST] round appears in Zodl's poll list, and Keystone users scan QR codes to register real notes into a test poll. (c) The coordinator flips `enable_for_new_rounds` on for a beta just before the final approval of a production round, which then becomes permanently proxy-enabled.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the public beta either on stage or under a separate beta dynamic-config channel and static pin that Zodl never reads. Before creating any mainnet test round, confirm what production Zodl does, and constrain mainnet test-round content to the strictest Zodl parser that has shipped. Make per-round enablement explicit and race-free, for example a one-shot `MsgSetProxyDelegationParams{enable_for_proposals_hash}` consumed at creation, or a MsgCreateVotingSession field added only in the activation commit. Add the beta schedule to the upgrade-window plan.

The Zodl evidence comes from a stale feature branch (a893c64a, 2026-05-13).

(b) is refuted. Every Zodl release with voting from 3.9.5 onward includes commit 576a979fd (2026-05-20). On the default config, the poll list shows only rounds in the Zodl endorsement set fetched from `/endorsed-rounds/zodl`. A signed [TEST] round that Zodl has not endorsed is therefore invisible to default-config Zodl users.

(a) is mostly fixed. Zodl 3.14.0 and later include commit 8a14c27c1 ('Accept 50-proposal rounds and skip a round that fails validation'). Only Zodl 3.13.x and earlier keep the parse-before-auth throw and the 1-15 proposal limit. That commit shows 50-proposal production rounds are planned anyway, so constraining round content for old Zodl is a general concern, not a proxy one. spec_rollout §3.4 already says not to sign mainnet [TEST] rounds into the prod config unless Zodl hides them.

(c) is a real sequencing footgun with low impact. Vizor also requires a signed per-round config extension, so a production round that is accidentally chain-enabled exposes nothing to Vizor users, and Zodl is unaffected by design. The reverse case only means no proxy delegation in that round. The upgrade-window point is already covered by the existing runbook check.

findings.title: The v1.7.0 release gate checks only VK fingerprints, but the chain's pin bump also replaces its non-circuit crypto stack

Moving to 0.13.0 also brings in voting-crypto-deps >=0.2.4, which pins zakura-primitives, zakura-reddsa, zakura-orchard and zakura-halo2-* =2.0.0 plus rand 0.10. The chain uses these for consensus checks outside the circuits: tx1_effects to sighash recomputation for ZKP1 (TxIdDigester), RedPallas verification, and tree hashing. The planned gate (ZKP1/2/3 VK fingerprints unchanged) does not exercise any of that. VK fingerprints also do not cover the FFI's public-input ordering. Today Vizor (Zakura 2.0) interoperates with the chain (Zakura 1.2), which is good evidence the digests agree, but the activation would be the first time the chain's own verifier changes stack, and Zodl's provers are never in the loop.

findings.title: Dormant-equivalence tests compare only ABCI codes, but GasUsed is also hashed, and the Msg-service gate is missing
findings.description: The chain spec plans for dormant v1.6.x binaries to be state-compatible, so they could ship in a rolling release, and its dormant tests assert only that rejections carry "the same ABCI code as v1.6.0". CometBFT hashes Code, Data, GasWanted and GasUsed into LastResultsHash. Vote txs run on an infinite gas meter but still report GasUsed equal to the KV gas consumed. Any extra KV read on an existing path in the dormant build therefore diverges LastResultsHash across mixed versions and halts consensus. Examples: reading ProxyDelegationParams in executeCreateVotingSession before checking the const, reading NextDelegateIndex in the reveal ante, or an extra round read. Decode errors are safe: BaseApp maps any decoder error to ErrTxDecode with gas 0, so tag-level dormancy is easy. Also, BaseApp needs a MsgServiceRouter handler for the new custom-wire messages, and that handler requires InterfaceRegistry resolution. The atomic-batch precedent therefore gated Msg-service registration (`RegisterMsgServerWithAtomicVoteBatchGate`), but the proxy dormant list gates only RegisterImplementations.

The next MsgApproveCoordinatorAction that creates a round reports a different GasUsed on upgraded and non-upgraded validators. LastResultsHash diverges, and the chain halts once more than 1/3 of validators disagree.
findings.proposed_fix: Either state that proxy dormant merges never ship in rolling releases, or add a harness that runs one block sequence (including every new tag, p=0 reveals, new Any payloads and round creation) through v1.6.0 and the dormant binary, and asserts identical full deterministic ExecTxResult (code, data, gas_wanted, gas_used), LastResultsHash and app hash. Add Msg-service method registration to the gated list, following the precedent.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified in code. CometBFT hashes GasUsed into LastResultsHash. BaseApp reports GasUsed from the ctx gas meter even on failures. The vote ante installs an infinite meter, which still accumulates consumed gas, and keeper KV access is gas-metered. Only decode failures report gas 0. One extra KV read before the dormant const check, on an existing accepted or rejected path, therefore changes GasUsed.

The rollout plans to label dormant PRs V:state/compatible, which allows a rolling replacement and backports. Yet the dormant tests compare only ABCI codes, and chain.md §9.3 reasons only about rejection codes. The integrated design also changes existing-path behavior: CheckNullifiersUnique becomes intra-message for all sets, which can change rejection order and codes on existing tags. That change must be gated too.

The Msg-service gate omission is real but fails loudly. Registering a method whose type URL is unresolved errors at startup, so it would not cause silent divergence.

findings.title: There is no chain-level brake on new DCs in an active round
findings.description: The per-round enable bit is an immutable snapshot, and the only coordinator knob is `enable_for_new_rounds`. The rollback plan is "disable for new rounds" plus the Vizor kill switch, but the kill switch does not stop third parties from submitting ZKP4 txs directly, and the upgrade runbook forbids halts while a round is in progress. ZKP4 is a new circuit at 98% row use. If a soundness or chain-handler bug is found mid-round, nothing can stop further exploitation until vote_end_time. The owner's finality decision is compatible with pausing new DCs, because existing DCs would stand.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:142 (snapshot), :133-135 (params), :48 (2,015/2,048 rows); specs/spec_rollout.md §7.1 (rollback is disable-for-new-rounds plus kill switch). [code] docs/runbooks/software-upgrades.md:476-479 ("Do not schedule the halt while a vote or ceremony is in progress").
findings.failure_scenario: Mid-round, an auditor finds that ZKP4 lets w exceed W. An attacker keeps submitting inflating DCs through REST until vote_end_time, and routing adds the inflated pools to the tally. The only remedy is an emergency halt that breaks the runbook's invariant, or accepting a corrupted result.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a coordinator-settable `proxy_dc_paused` param that applies to all rounds immediately. It is checked in ante and DeliverTx for DC actions and in the p=0 branch of MsgRevealShare only for DCs included after the pause height, if that is cheaply identifiable; otherwise for DC submission only. Document it in the incident runbook and test it with Zodl flows unaffected.

verdict.reasoning:
It is true that nothing can stop new DCs in an active round. However, this matches today's posture for every vote message. The closed coordinator payload set has no cancel or pause for ZKP1, ZKP2 or ZKP3 either, so the gap is not specific to proxy delegation.

The proposed brake is also weaker than it looks:
- It cannot undo inflating DCs that are already included.
- It needs threshold approvals, so an attacker can race it.
- The p=0 reveal variant cannot be implemented, because DC reveals are deliberately unlinkable to DC inclusion height.

A DC-submission pause is cheap defense in depth for a new circuit at 98% row use, but it is optional hardening rather than a design blocker.
verdict.evidence: [code] x/vote/keeper/msg_server_coordinator_actions.go:17-31 (payloads: create session, vote managers, schedule and cancel upgrade, endorser, authorized send; no round pause or cancel). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:824 (rollback covers new rounds only plus the kill switch); integrated-design-v1.md:48, :142, :221 (reveal times unlinkable to the DC); vote-sdk docs/runbooks/software-upgrades.md:476-479.
verdict.refined_fix: Optional: add a coordinator `proxy_dc_paused` flag, checked in the ante and DeliverTx for 0x09 DC actions only. Leave reveals and routes alone, so existing DCs stand under the owner's finality decision. Document it in the incident runbook with a test showing that Zodl flows are unaffected. Put the larger effort into the ZKP4 audit and conservation tests.

findings.title: Three specs disagree on the IAVL key layout, and a non-membership proof turns a mismatch into a false "did not vote"
findings.description: Light-client keys are effectively consensus-adjacent, but the specs disagree on them. The integrated design puts routes at `0x1B||round||u32(d)`, the routing base at 0x1C and params at 0x1D. The chain spec (authoritative for detail) puts the key index at 0x1B, routes at 0x1C, params at 0x1D, NextDelegateIndex at 0x1E and the routing base at 0x1F. The identity spec uses 0x1A sub-prefixes (0x1A01 record, 0x1A02 key index, and so on). Vizor proves both membership and non-membership, and after TALLYING it shows "did not vote" for a route that is proven absent. A wallet that derives keys from a different spec than the chain gets a valid proof of absence under the wrong key, with no error.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:139-140; specs/chain.md §5.1 table and §5.4 (routes 0x1C, record 0x1A||u32); specs/identity.md:382-392 (0x1A 0x01 record, 0x1A 0x02 key index, ...); specs/vizor.md:701-713 ("Route absent after TALLYING: prove non-membership").
findings.failure_scenario: The chain implements the integrated layout with routes at 0x1B, while Vizor's Rust reader follows the chain-spec contract and queries 0x1C||round||d. At 0x1C there is only routing-base data with longer keys, so the absence proof verifies, and every delegator sees "@alice did not vote (abstained)" on proposals Alice routed. The same mismatch on the record key would make delegates look unregistered or revoked.
findings.proposed_fix: Put one normative key table in ZIP-PD/ZIP-DR with golden key-derivation vectors that both the chain's keys.go tests and Vizor's participation reader consume. Have ProtocolCapabilities expose a `proxy_state_layout_version`, and fail closed if it does not match.

verdict.reasoning:
The specs give conflicting state layouts:
- Integrated design: routes at 0x1B||round||d, routing base at 0x1C, params at 0x1D, and a 0x1A family that also holds params.
- Chain spec: key index at 0x1B, routes at 0x1C, params at 0x1D, NextDelegateIndex at 0x1E, routing base at 0x1F. It also says wallets prove routes at 0x1C.
- Identity spec: 0x1A sub-prefixes.

The Vizor spec adds a fourth layout and makes the bug concrete. It proves a per-proposal key `DelegateRoute{round_id, delegate_index, proposal_id}`, but both chain layouts store one route set per (round, d). A per-proposal key never exists, so its non-membership proof always verifies, and Vizor would show 'Didn't vote ... Verified' for proposals the delegate did route. An absence proof under the wrong key succeeds silently, so mocked unit tests will not catch it. The layout must be settled before three teams implement it in parallel.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:139-140; specs/chain.md:405-410 (layout table), :479-480 (wallets prove 0x1A||d and 0x1C||round||d), :504,516; specs/identity.md:382-392; specs/vizor.md:226 ('Didn't vote ... Verified once non-membership is proved'), :703 (per-proposal DelegateRoute key kind), :707 (route absent after TALLYING: prove non-membership).
verdict.refined_fix: Put one normative key table in ZIP-DR/ZIP-PD, with golden key-derivation vectors consumed by both the chain's keys.go tests and Vizor's participation reader. Define route absence as a proven membership of the (round, d) route set and then parsing it, or as non-membership of that whole set key. It must never be shown through a per-proposal key. Add a stage e2e check that a routed proposal shows as Voted through the IAVL path. A layout version in ProtocolCapabilities is optional.

findings.title: The V2 acceptance list misses the size and cap coupling: one global 15 KiB proof constant, a 50-action envelope and a reveal cap on tag 0x04 only
findings.description: V2's ZKP1.5 proof (57.7 KiB, so 64.7 KiB per cast bundle) does not break B2 by itself, but it exposes three assumptions in the integrated plan. (a) MaxProofSize is one constant used by every ValidateBasic, including MsgRevealShare and the planned DC actions, and by the 15 KiB FFI prove buffer. V2 must therefore raise it per circuit rather than globally, or B2's DC and pool-reveal checks loosen too. (b) The 0x09 envelope (`max_vote_actions_per_tx=50`, "same as today's 50-cast composite", oneof 3..9 reserved for V2 casts) holds only about 11 V2 casts under the Comet RPC body cap, so packing must be by byte budget and the atomic "delegations plus own votes per VAN" UX cannot hold in V2 rounds. (c) The 256-per-block reveal cap counts only tag 0x04. Once V2 moves vote reveals to a new tag, pool reveals (0x04) and direct reveals are no longer jointly capped, which undoes the fairness argument in §4.1. In addition, ProtocolCapabilities' fixed "ZKP1-4 fingerprint" fields cannot describe V2 rounds, which need both the v1 and v2 ZKP3. These are V2 work items, but they belong in the coordination plan the design commits to.

V2 casts packed into 0x09 at the advertised 50-action limit exceed the REST and RPC caps and are rejected at the vote server. V2 direct reveals on the new tag are uncapped, while pool reveals still compete for 256 per block.

findings.title: The specs disagree on a per-block proof-verification cap; any cap must not strand Zodl's 51-proof batches
findings.description: spec_rollout says a per-block proof-action cap ships in the activation, the chain spec says none is needed, and the integrated design caps only registry ops. Proof-heavy blocks already exist today with 0x06 and 0x07, and ZKP4 adds the same class of load (bounded per registration by the 16 slots). If a cap is added, a value below 51 makes Zodl's maximal 0x07 (ZKP1 + 50 casts) impossible to include ever. A cap that counts txs instead of proofs, or orders new tags first, can delay Zodl's batches behind DC batches.
findings.evidence: [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md §0 item 4 and §3.2; specs/chain.md §8 ("No new cap is needed"); integrated-design-v1.md:120. [measured] ZKP2 verify takes 1.8-2.0 ms on an M3 Ultra (28 cores), and a 5 MiB block holds about 460 proofs, roughly 0.9 s per block on that machine. Validator SKUs are 2-4 vCPU droplets (docs/production-setup.md:19-20,222-223), so expect several seconds per full block [inference].
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds a cap of 32 proof actions per block. A Zodl user's ZKP1 + 50 casts tx (51 proofs) sits in the mempool forever, Zodl shows the vote as pending, and it expires at vote_end_time.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide explicitly. If a cap is added, express it in verification weight, keep it at least the maximum single-tx proof count (51, or 66 at the RPC byte cap), keep FIFO across old and new tags, and add a load-lab case with Zodl 0x07 batches during a DC burst.

findings.title: The helper checks the delegate index before the DC leaf and makes "unknown index" a permanent error
findings.description: The helper's ingress runs validateShareChoice, which would include the new `1 <= d < NextDelegateIndex` p=0 branch and return a 400, before verifyCommitment checks that the DC leaf exists. The design makes unknown indices a "permanent, distinct error". A helper node a few blocks behind the registration, which can still pass the staleness gate, will permanently refuse an honest DC share that it would accept after catching up.
findings.evidence: [code] internal/helper/api.go:337-357 (validateShareChoice; ErrInvalidRoundChoice is a 400) runs before :359-384 (verifyCommitment); cmd/svoted/cmd/helper.go:310-341 (choice validator reads the node's latest committed state); api.go:618-624 (staleness gate only). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:167.
findings.failure_scenario: A delegate registers at height N, and a delegator's DC lands at N+2. A helper whose node has the leaf in its cache but evaluates NextDelegateIndex at an older committed view (or one that lags at ingress) returns a permanent 400. The wallet does not retry that helper, and with single-helper delivery the share and its ballots never reach Pool[d].
findings.proposed_fix: For p=0, run verifyCommitment first. A present DC leaf proves the helper's view is at or after the DC height, so `d >= NextDelegateIndex` is then truly permanent. If the leaf is absent, return the existing retryable unavailable status.

findings.title: `GET /tally/{round}/0` still exposes every pool as one unpaginated map; the chain spec's fix was dropped
findings.description: ProposalTally iterates `TallyKey(round, proposal_id, *)` for any proposal_id, including 0. The chain spec said ProposalTally must reject proposal 0, but the integrated design's list of old APIs touched by proposal 0 omits it. The ciphertexts are public state anyway, so this is not a confidentiality break. It is still a proposal-0 leak into an old API, an unbounded response (64 B times the number of delegates per call on an unauthenticated REST API), and a trap for explorers that iterate `0..len(proposals)`.
findings.evidence: [code] api/query_handler.go:59,184-208; x/vote/keeper/query_server.go:118-135; x/vote/keeper/keeper_tally.go:99-129. [doc] specs/chain.md §5.3 ("ProposalTally must reject proposal_id == 0"); integrated-design-v1.md:131.
findings.failure_scenario: An explorer or monitoring script calls /tally/{round}/0. It receives 10k entries that look like options of a proposal 0, shows phantom options, or times out under load.
findings.proposed_fix: Have ProposalTally reject proposal_id 0 (and ids above len(proposals)), and serve pools only through the paged `delegate-pools` query.

findings.title: The routing EndBlock cost is benchmarked in memory on an M3 Ultra and is not bounded by any parameter
findings.description: The 1.4 s figure for 10k delegates × 50 proposals comes from an in-memory benchmark with pre-decoded pools and no IAVL reads, run on an M3 Ultra. The real hook adds, per delegate, an IAVL read of the route set plus protobuf decode, and an IAVL read of the pool plus two point decompressions. The work is Σ routes over delegates with pools, bounded only by registry size (identity `max_delegates` = 1,000,000). Validators are 2-4 vCPU droplets, and the routing block's FinalizeBlock is single-threaded. This is not a halt risk (the errors are corruption-only), but it is an unbudgeted stall of several seconds or more, in the same block where TALLYING starts.
findings.evidence: [code] proto-chain/route_test.go:186-205 (pools pre-decoded, no KV); docs/production-setup.md:19-20,222-223 (s-2vcpu-8gb-amd and s-4vcpu-16gb-amd validators). [doc] specs/identity.md ProxyDelegateParams.max_delegates default 1,000,000. [measured] review-chainops/decomp at GOMAXPROCS=1 on an M3 Ultra: UnmarshalCiphertext + add = 44.9 µs and add = 1.88 µs, so 10k pools need 0.45 s of decoding plus 0.94 s of adds before IAVL I/O.
findings.failure_scenario: A popular round has 20k routed delegates. The TALLYING-transition block takes roughly 6-10 s to finalize on 2-vCPU validators. If future growth or a cheaper registration path pushes the count to about 100k, block production stalls for about a minute at every tally.
findings.proposed_fix: Benchmark the real keeper hook against IAVL on the production droplet class and add it to CI with an alert. Set `max_delegates` and an explicit routed-pairs budget from that number. If needed, spread routing deterministically over the first K TALLYING blocks and delay partial-decrypt injection until a `pools_routed` flag is set.

findings.title: delegate_index_bound fits K=11 for free, but its bit width and value rule must be fixed before implementation
findings.description: O1 is resolved: the in-circuit check `1 <= d <= bound` costs no extra rows, no proof bytes and no prove time at K=11, so it should be included. The integrated design (section 3, O1) still leaves two decisions open, and each one matters. (a) Bit width. The task suggests 2^20. A 20-bit check bakes a hard limit of about 1M delegate indices into the ZKP4 VK. An open registry with free GitHub and DNS providers could plausibly reach that over the life of the VK, and raising it later is a VK bump. The 30-bit (3-word) check costs exactly the same. (b) The bound value. `bound` is public and the circuit enforces `d <= bound`. If the builder lets the caller choose it freely, a lazy or buggy client that sets `bound = d` (or any tight bound) reveals the target delegate at DC tx time. That breaks the section 8 claim that the target of a DC is hidden at DC tx time. (c) The public-input count goes from 11 to 12, so the FFI buffer (352 to 384 B), ProtocolCapabilities and the frozen vectors must be updated.
findings.evidence: [measured] Variants are in review-circuit_feasibility/voting-circuits/src/proxy_delegation/circuit_bound.rs (synth_bound :803-845, custom gate :339). They witness e1=d-1 and e2=bound-d (bound copied from instance offset 11) and run strict `copy_check` on both with 2, 3 or 4 words. Every variant gives max_rows 2015/2048 (unchanged), advice 34, lookups 4, perm 44, and fixed 78 for the gate or gated-AddChip variant. Real proofs are 11,008 B, the same as baseline. The 11,040 B seen in some AddChip runs came from a stray unused selector and disappears once that selector is gated. Interleaved prove medians at 8 threads: 94.6-95.5 ms vs baseline 94.9-95.3 ms. Verify is about 1.62-1.69 ms. The soundness suites (tests_bound.rs:101-129, 184) accept d=1, d=bound and d=bound=2^B-1. They reject d=0, d=bound+1, instance bound<d, d-1=2^B, bound-d=2^B and d=p-1. Changing PI[11] makes a real proof fail. ZKP1 already uses the same `nb_minus_one` encoding (vc/src/delegation/circuit.rs:1364-1374).
findings.failure_scenario: (b) A client implements `bound := delegate_index` (it satisfies the circuit and the chain rule `bound < NextDelegateIndex`). Every DC tx then publishes its delegate index in clear, and an observer links each anonymous batch to its delegates and its timing. (a) With 2^20, once the registry passes 1,048,576 entries, no client can delegate to any new delegate until a VK change.
findings.proposed_fix: Adopt the 3-word (30-bit) encoding: e1=d-1, e2=bound-d, both strict 3x10-bit lookup range checks, plus a one-row custom gate or two AddChip rows (both measured free). The builder API should take the chain-authenticated `NextDelegateIndex`, not a free `bound`, and set bound = NextDelegateIndex-1. The chain accepts iff `bound < NextDelegateIndex`, which stays true between proving and inclusion because the registry is append-only. Optionally also require `bound >= NextDelegateIndexAtRoundCreation-1` as a public floor, so a buggy client cannot narrow the range. Cap the registry at 2^30. Update public inputs to 12 in FFI, capabilities and vectors.

verdict.reasoning:
The measurement holds and settles O1: the bound check is free at K=11, so it should go in. The three sub-claims are weaker than stated, though, so this is spec cleanup rather than a design change.

(a) Bit width. The failure scenario cannot happen under the current specs. The identity spec already caps the registry at `max_delegates` = 1,000,000, which is below 2^20 (identity.md:335; register requires `next_index <= max_delegates`, :366). The verifier also limits issuance to 500 registrations a day across all users (identity.md:485), so reaching 1M would take more than 5 years. A 20-bit check therefore matches the identity spec today. The real gap is different. `max_delegates` is a coordinator-mutable param, and nothing ties it to the circuit width. The chain spec has no registry cap at all, and the integrated design only says "caps". If a coordinator ever raised the cap above 2^B, the damage would be worse than the finding says. With `bound = Next-1`, any d where `Next-1-d >= 2^B` fails the `e2` range check, so delegation to older, low-index delegates breaks as well, and it stays broken until a VK change, because the index count cannot shrink. Choosing 30 bits costs nothing, so it is the better choice, but the essential fix is a consensus invariant: max index <= 2^B.

(b) The bound value. The chain spec already states the rule: "REQUIRES from client: set delegate_index_bound = NextDelegateIndex-1, read from an IAVL-verified or trusted state" (chain.summary.md:39, with the leak-free rationale at :5). What is missing is that client.md never mentions the bound and the integrated design does not carry the rule over. A client built from those two documents could pick `bound = d`. This is a gap in passing the rule between specs, not a missing design. The proposed floor `bound >= NextAtRoundCreation-1` only partly helps: it does nothing for delegates registered mid-round, because `bound = d` still passes the floor for them. It is optional defense in depth, not a fix.

(c) The 12th public input is a mechanical consequence. The chain spec already includes `DelegateIndexBound` in `ProxyDelegationInputs` (chain.md:732). It puts the bound at instance position 7, while the prototype appends it at position 11, so one canonical order needs to be fixed.

One caveat on "both measured free": the plain AddChip variants (PLACE 0) measured 79 fixed columns and an 11,040 B proof. Only the custom-gate variants (PLACE 3/4) and the PLACE 5 variant gave 78 columns and 11,008 B. The reviewer's stray-selector explanation is plausible, but only the custom gate was measured directly at 11,008 B without that caveat.
verdict.evidence:
[measured] I re-ran the reviewer's prototype from a copy in scratchpad/review-circuit_feasibility-skeptic, using `cargo test --release --lib bound_ -- --include-ignored`. All 12 tests pass.
- Row budget: every variant (20, 30 and 40 bits) reports max_rows=2015, advice_cols=34, lookups=4, perm_cols=44. Fixed columns are 79 for PLACE 0-2 (AddChip) and 78 for PLACE 3/4 (custom gate) and PLACE 5.
- Real proofs: the 30-bit custom gate (w3_p4) gives 11,008 B, the 30-bit PLACE 5 variant gives 11,008 B, and the 30-bit plain AddChip (w3_p0) gives 11,040 B.
- Prove medians are within noise of the baseline (about 64-66 ms on both sides, default thread count). Verify takes about 2.0 ms.
- The soundness suites w2_p0, w2_p3, w3_p0, w3_p5 and w4_p0 pass, including the rejections of d=0, d=bound+1, d-1=2^B, bound-d=2^B and d=p-1.

[code] circuit_bound.rs:803-844 (synth_bound with strict `copy_check` on e1=d-1 and e2=bound-d), :339-347 (custom gate). tests_bound.rs:117-120 shows d=2^B is accepted and bound-d=2^B is rejected, so `bound=Next-1` breaks for low d once `Next-1 >= 2^B + d`.

[code] vc/src/delegation/circuit.rs:1363-1374 uses the same `nb_minus_one` 3-word encoding, as the finding says.

[doc]
- identity.md:335 caps `max_delegates` at 1,000,000 (< 2^20); :366 requires `next_index <= max_delegates`; :481-485 sets the verifier's global cap of 500/day; :344 shows `MsgSetProxyDelegateParams` with no rule tying `max_delegates` to the circuit width.
- chain.md:300-309 sets params with no registry cap. chain.md:16, :132 and :141 require `bound < NextDelegateIndex`. chain.md:740 puts the bound at instance position 7.
- chain.summary.md:39 has the client rule `bound = NextDelegateIndex-1`; client.md has no matching rule (grep for bound/NextDelegateIndex finds nothing).
- integrated-design-v1.md §3 lists 11 public inputs and leaves O1 open.
verdict.refined_fix:
1. Circuits: adopt the 3-word (30-bit) check, `e1 = d-1` and `e2 = bound-d`, each with a strict 3x10-bit lookup range check. Implement it as the one-row custom gate, which was measured directly at 78 fixed columns and an 11,008 B proof. Re-measure rows and proof size after every other ZKP4 change lands, because the 33-row headroom (2015/2048) is shared.

2. Chain consensus invariant: the highest assignable index must be at most 2^30. Validate `max_delegates <= 2^30` in the params message and check `next_index <= min(max_delegates, 2^30)` on register, so a param change can never make `bound = Next-1` unprovable.

3. Client: copy the chain spec's existing rule into client.md and the integrated design. The ZKP4 builder takes the IAVL-verified `NextDelegateIndex`, read immediately before proving (the pre-proving cross-check already reads it), and sets `bound = NextDelegateIndex - 1` internally. The public API exposes no free `bound` parameter. Add a test that the bound never equals d unless `d = Next-1`. A chain-side floor is optional defense in depth and does not cover delegates registered mid-round.

4. Choose one public-input order (append the bound at position 11 after `dc_slot_nf`, or follow the chain spec's position 7), use it in FFI (`12 x 32 = 384 B`), `ProtocolCapabilities`/VK fingerprint and the vectors, and record O1 as resolved.

findings.title: After full delegation, the W=0 successor VAN can still cast zero-weight ZKP2 votes
findings.description: ZKP4 allows W_new=0 ('delegate everything'), which creates a new kind of VAN: weight 0 with the MAX mask. Today no such VAN exists, because ZKP1 forces num_ballots >= 1. ZKP2 has no W != 0 gate, so this VAN can still produce up to 50 valid zero-weight vote commitments. Each one triggers 16 helper ZKP3 reveals and shows up as a vote in ShareCount/VoteSummary-style counts. The tally is unaffected and no weight is lost. However, the per-registration helper load bound rises from 800 to 16x16 + 50x16 = 1,056 shares. A client that runs its normal cast flow after 'delegate everything' would also show the user zero-weight 'votes'.
findings.evidence: [measured] review_chain_tests.rs:150-175 (`review_full_delegation_then_zero_weight`). Full delegation passes MockProver. A further ZKP4 from W=0 is rejected at the C7 3-word range check. The unchanged `build_vote_proof_from_delegation(total=0, MAX)` produces a real ZKP2 proof whose root is SingleLeafRoot(W=0 successor), and `verify_vote_proof` returns Ok. [code] ZKP2 uses NonZeroConfig only for El Gamal randomness (vc/src/vote_proof/circuit.rs:1354,1374). ZKP1 enforces num_ballots in [1,2^30] (vc/src/delegation/circuit.rs:1364-1374).
findings.failure_scenario: Vizor's combined review computes the remainder W-w=0 but still submits own-vote casts, or a scripted client does it on purpose. 50 zero-weight VCs land, helpers do 800 extra reveals, and explorers and status screens count votes that carry no weight.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not change the ZKP2 VK. Treat a W=0 VAN as terminal: the planner and packer refuse casts from it, and the status view shows 'all delegated'. State in ZIP-PD that a zero-weight successor is dead by convention. Add the W=0 to ZKP2 real-proof case to the test list so the behaviour is deliberate.

findings.title: The 16-DC slot cap depends on rand never changing along MAX-preserving transitions
findings.description: The slot nullifier is Poseidon4(nk, TAG+slot, round, rand). It is unique per registration chain only because every transition that keeps the MAX mask (ZKP4 C6) reuses the same rand cell, and the only other VAN transition (ZKP2) removes MAX. This holds today. However, the design's own research floats VAN split, merge and re-randomization circuits (to fix successor traceability). Any future circuit that outputs a MAX VAN with a fresh rand would silently reset the cap, and each re-randomization would buy 16 more DCs. The intra-batch slot-nf dedupe is a separate prerequisite. Today's intra-batch VAN-nf dedupe lives in ValidateBasic, not in CheckNullifiersUnique. The handler calls CheckNullifiersUnique (store-only) and then SetNullifier blindly, so a new message that only extends CheckNullifiersUnique would still accept repeated slot nfs within one tx.
findings.evidence: [code] prototype C6 reuses the `van_comm_rand` cell (proto circuit.rs:545-557) and C14 (:520-543). ZKP2 reuses rand (vc/src/vote_proof/circuit.rs:1112-1123), and the private-vote branch also keeps `van_comm_rand_cond6` (git show origin/roman/private-vote-implementation:src/vote_proof/circuit.rs:779,1017). The batch handler does store-only check then blind set (vs/x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:242-249). Intra-batch dedupe is only in ValidateBasic (vs/x/vote/types/msgs.go:180-204). [measured] review_chain_tests.rs:107-147: 16 distinct slot nfs per chain, disjoint across a second bundle (different rand) and another round. Reusing a slot later in the chain reproduces the identical nf.
findings.failure_scenario: (1) A later 'VAN refresh/split' circuit preserves MAX but draws a new rand. A whale then cycles refresh then 16 DCs repeatedly, multiplying helper load. (2) The 0x09 ValidateBasic forgets the seen-set for slot nfs. One batch carries 10 DCs all using slot 0, and the cap becomes 16x10 = 160 DCs per chain.
findings.proposed_fix: Write 'rand is invariant along every MAX-mask transition' into ZIP-PD as a normative invariant, with a cross-circuit test. Any future VAN-transforming circuit must either keep rand or carry a slot counter. Put slot-nf (and VAN-nf) intra-message dedupe in the 0x09 ValidateBasic, mirroring msgs.go:180-204, and add a negative chain test with a duplicate slot nf inside one batch.

findings.title: The ZKP4 proving key adds about 140 MiB, and the integrated design does not require sequential loading
findings.description: Time is not the problem. ZKP4 proves as fast as ZKP2 (measured 0.53 s single-thread and 0.16 s at 4 threads on M3 Ultra), and the spec's 'several seconds per DC on phones' is likely pessimistic. Memory is the issue. The ZKP4 proving key costs the same as ZKP2's. With ZKP4, ZKP2 and ZKP3 all resident, peak RSS is 259 MiB, and ZKP1's 156 MB key plus 26 MiB of prepared tables push a fully warmed client to about 440 MiB. The circuits spec has 'evict ZKP4 pk after use' (C5), but integrated design section 5 and the Vizor section omit it. Low-RAM Android devices are the risk.
findings.evidence: [measured] /usr/bin/time -l maximum resident set size: keygen_only_zkp4 146,833,408 B; keygen_only_zkp2 141,164,544 B; review_keygen_all_resident (ZKP4+ZKP2+ZKP3) 271,532,032 B. ZKP1 pk is 156 MB plus 26.4 MiB tables per dossiers/circuits.md:133. Thread scaling (review_chain_tests.rs:245-281) gives ZKP4 prove 530/278/161/96 ms at 1/2/4/8 threads vs ZKP2 build+prove 536/283/166/98 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: Vizor warms all keys at app start (as `warm_*` APIs encourage). On a 3-4 GB Android phone, a ZKP1 + 10 DC + 50 cast session holds about 440 MiB of keys plus proving buffers, and the OS kills the app mid-batch, so a partially signed plan has to be recovered.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the integrated design (section 5, client) normative: prove in phases ZKP1, then all ZKP4s, then ZKP2s. Load each key only for its phase and drop it before the next. Never pre-warm ZKP4 at app start. Add a peak-RSS budget to the device benchmark gate (client spec item 14).

findings.title: Replay is prevented, but the sighash needs a per-action kind tag, and the embedded registration can still be split off
findings.description: Proofs cannot be moved to another batch, round or anchor (see confirmations). Two residual gaps remain. (1) SVOTE_VOTE_ACTION_BATCH_SIGHASH_V1 mixes DC entries (r_vpk, van_nf, van_new, dc, slot_nf, hint) and cast entries (r_vpk, van_nf, van_new, vc, proposal_id) in one ordered list. Unlike the existing cast-only digests, it needs an explicit per-action kind byte and a fixed per-kind layout so the encoding is unambiguous. (2) The optional registration keeps its own self-contained signature, which the batch digest deliberately excludes, as today. A relayer or validator can therefore lift the MsgDelegateVote out of a pending 0x09 batch and submit it alone. The registration lands, and the batch then fails on the spent gov nullifiers. This is pre-existing for MsgDelegateAndCastVoteBatch, but it now strands planned DCs.
findings.evidence: [code] the existing digests hash fixed 5-field cast entries with no kind tag (vs/x/vote/types/sighash.go:77-132). The composite excludes the delegation proof and signature (sighash.go:104-107) and verifies the delegation with the standalone verifier (vs/x/vote/ante/validate.go:184-243). [measured] On a real ZKP4 proof, incrementing any one of the 11 PIs, including anchor_height (PI[6], which is only transcript-bound), makes verification fail, and the ZKP4 proof fails under the ZKP2 VK even though both take 11 PIs (review_chain_tests.rs:177-243).
findings.failure_scenario: (2) An adversarial relayer unbundles a 'ZKP1 + 10 DCs + casts' batch. The VAN appears in the tree on its own and the batch is rejected. A client that assumes 0x09 is atomic marks the DCs as failed, or retries with the synthetic anchor forever, instead of re-planning against the real anchor.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the 0x09 digest as domain || round || anchor_height || has_registration || van_cmx? || n || for each action (index, kind byte, fixed per-kind fields), and include delegate_index_bound if CF-1 is adopted. In the client recovery state machine, treat 'registration landed, batch rejected' as a normal transition: re-plan the same DCs and casts anchored at the real tree (the VAN still has the MAX mask, so ZKP4 still works).

confirmations: [code] The chain appends the final VAN first, then each commitment in action order (x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:250-262). The chain, client and integrated docs are correct; spec_rollout ZIP-PD is wrong.
[code] KV prefixes 0x1A-0x1F are unused (x/vote/types/keys.go:114-207). Nullifier types 0x00-0x02 are in use and 0x03 is free (keys.go:98-107). Nullifier values are just []byte{1} (keys.go:113).
[code] ProtocolCapabilities has only fields 1-3 today (proto/svote/v1/query.proto:73-77), so appending fields is safe once numbers are coordinated.
[code] IsVoteTag is a contiguous 0x02-0x07 range and 0x0A is forbidden (api/codec.go:25-26, 57-59), so the new tags need explicit branches, as the specs say.
[code] Helper share payloads carry vc_tree_position (zcash_voting src/share.rs:1026, 1091), so shares are delivered only after inclusion.
[code] One immediate share per round is designated by round_immediate_share_key (zcash_voting src/share_policy/initial_placement.rs:30-39).

[code] In the local Zodl checkout (a893c64a), round JSON is parsed as [String: Any] (VotingAPIClientLiveKey.swift:574-588) and dynamic config via Codable (VotingServiceConfig.swift:6-58), so extra keys are ignored. That checkout has no [TEST] filtering.
[code] Vizor hides [TEST]-prefixed rounds (voting_round_visibility_provider.dart:13-17). Every Vizor config switch kind invalidates the same state (voting_config_provider.dart:200-214).
[code] VoteSummary iterates round.Proposals and its BallotCount is the share count (keeper_tally.go:197-209), so proposal 0 never appears there.
[code] The REST body limit is 1 MiB (api/handler.go io.LimitReader 1<<20) and the block max is 5 MiB (app/consensus_limits.go:13).

[doc] The integrated doc correctly adopts identity's rule of no X content on chain and the client's (d,w,layout)-bound dc_seed. The planner and Vizor editor cover the original asks: up to 10 delegates, keep some, delegate everything. 'Did my delegate vote' is covered by the whole-round route list, IAVL proofs and the per-proposal status view.

findings.title: Integrated registry lets the hot DRK undo a freeze, which defeats the cold-DIK emergency brake
findings.description: Integrated §4.1 lists `freeze` / `unfreeze` (DIK or DRK). The identity spec it claims to follow makes freeze one-way for the DRK: FROZEN can only be undone by a DIK-signed route-key rotation. The whole reason for having a separate DRK is that a leaked hot key can be contained. If a DRK can also unfreeze, an attacker holding the stolen DRK simply unfreezes and routes, so freeze contains nothing.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:117 `freeze / unfreeze (DIK or DRK)`. [doc] specs/identity.md:116 Freeze is signed by DIK or DRK and is `Undone only by a route-key rotation (DIK)`; identity.md:129 response matrix: `freeze with DRK then rotate later`. [doc] identity.md:316 has no UNFREEZE op in the oneof.
findings.failure_scenario: A delegate's phone (holding the DRK) is stolen mid-round. The owner freezes with a second device. The thief signs `unfreeze` with the same DRK, then routes every unrouted proposal against the owner's positions. Routes are final (decision 2), so the whole pool is captured.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the `unfreeze` op. FROZEN goes back to ACTIVE only through `rotate_route_key`, which the DIK signs and which burns the old DRK. The DRK may only freeze and cancel_pending. Add a chain test that a DRK-signed unfreeze, or any route signed by the pre-rotation DRK after a freeze, is rejected.

verdict.reasoning: This is real. Integrated §4.1 lets either the DIK or the DRK sign both freeze and unfreeze. The identity spec makes freeze one-way: only a DIK route-key rotation turns FROZEN back to ACTIVE, and the identity proto oneof has no unfreeze op. A DRK-signed unfreeze turns the DRK freeze into a race the thief always wins. The case that matters is a cold DIK with the DRK on two devices: the owner freezes with the DRK, the thief unfreezes with the same DRK, and the thief routes before the owner can reach the DIK. Routes are final, so the whole pool's weight is misdirected. DIK rotation is still immediate, but that does not help while the DIK is out of reach. A DIK-only unfreeze would also be unsafe, because it leaves the stolen DRK live.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:117 `freeze / unfreeze (DIK or DRK)`. [doc] specs/identity.md:112 (rotate route key: FROZEN becomes ACTIVE), :116 (freeze is `Undone only by a route-key rotation (DIK)`), :129, :285-294 (oneof has register, rotate_route_key, change_identity, recover_identity, cancel_pending, freeze and revoke, with no unfreeze), :377 (freeze precondition is status ACTIVE).
verdict.refined_fix: Remove `unfreeze` from integrated §4.1. FROZEN returns to ACTIVE only through `rotate_route_key`, which the DIK signs and which bumps key_epoch so that every signature from the old DRK dies. The DRK may only sign freeze and cancel_pending. Add chain tests for two cases: no op signed by the pre-freeze DRK can return the entry to ACTIVE, and a route signed by the pre-rotation DRK is rejected after a rotation.

findings.title: Vizor's 'Stop accepting delegations' maps to a status that blocks routes, so delegators silently abstain
findings.description: Vizor DG-11 maps 'Stop accepting delegations' to `MsgSetDelegateStatus(inactive)` and tells the delegate 'You can still vote publicly in rounds already in progress.' That promise fails on two counts. First, `MsgSetDelegateStatus` is a coordinator-only payload in the chain spec, so a delegate cannot send it. Second, the only delegate-signed equivalent, freeze, rejects routes in both the identity spec and the integrated spec. The chain also cannot stop new delegations, because `d` is hidden inside the DC. So 'stop accepting' can only ever be an off-chain listing signal.
findings.evidence: [doc] specs/vizor.md:416 (copy and message), :615 `delegate_build_status`. [doc] specs/chain.md:301-312: MsgSetDelegateStatus is a coordinator payload via MsgProposeCoordinatorAction. [doc] identity.md:116 and integrated-design-v1.md:126: a route requires effective ACTIVE, not frozen. [doc] identity.md:442: the chain cannot reject delegations to frozen delegates.
findings.failure_scenario: A popular delegate taps 'Stop accepting delegations' on day 2 of a 7-day round, trusting the copy. If this is implemented as freeze, every later route is rejected and every delegator's weight abstains on all unrouted proposals. Delegations are final, so delegators cannot react.
findings.proposed_fix: Map 'Stop accepting delegations' to the DIK-signed delegate statement with `accepting:false` (identity.md:257). The publisher shows 'Not accepting', and the client refuses new DCs at preview, commit and pre-prove. Chain status does not change and routes keep working. Rename freeze in the UI to 'Emergency pause' and state that it blocks your public votes and that delegators abstain on proposals you have not voted on. Remove `delegate_build_status` from the Vizor bridge.

verdict.reasoning: Vizor DG-11 maps 'Stop accepting delegations' to `MsgSetDelegateStatus(inactive)`. That message is a coordinator payload, and its status can only be ACTIVE or SUSPENDED. The integrated registry has no delegate-signed status of that kind; the only one a delegate can sign is freeze, and freeze rejects routes. The chain also cannot block new DCs to a delegate, because d is hidden in the DC. So the button has no backing operation. Its copy ('no one can delegate to you', 'you can still vote publicly') is only true if the action is an off-chain listing flag. Delegators lose weight only if someone wires the button to freeze, which is plausible but not certain, so this is a spec gap, not yet a hole. Identity already has an off-chain `accepting` field in the DIK-signed statement. However, its listing rules (identity.md:571) do not use that field yet.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/vizor.md:416-417, :470, and :612 (`delegate_build_status`). [doc] specs/chain.md:296-312 (MsgSetDelegateStatus is a coordinator payload; status is ACTIVE or SUSPENDED). [doc] specs/identity.md:41 (UI 'Pause delegate voting' = Freeze), :116, :257 (`accepting` in the statement), :442 (the chain cannot reject delegations), :571 (the lookup_only rule has no `accepting` condition). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:126.
verdict.refined_fix: Map 'Stop accepting' and 'Resume accepting' to a new DIK-signed statement with `accepting:false` or `true`. Add `accepting=false` to identity's listing and lookup_only rules, and have the client refuse new allocations to such delegates at preview, commit and pre-prove. Chain status and routes are unaffected. Change the copy to 'Vizor will stop offering you as a delegate'; it is not an on-chain guarantee. Remove `delegate_build_status` from the Vizor bridge. Label freeze 'Emergency pause' and say that unrouted proposals will abstain.

findings.title: Client and Vizor registration shapes would write X user ids and handles into permanent tx bytes
findings.description: The integrated design and the identity spec put only a salted `subject_commit` on chain, so that X data can be shredded within 24 h. The client spec's `MsgRegisterDelegate{dk_pubkey, attestations, pop_sig}` carries `DelegateAttestationV1`, which contains `provider_user_id`, `provider_handle` and `proof_locator`. Vizor DG-6 submits a 'DK-signed registration statement including `x_user_id`'. Tx bytes are kept forever, and blocks are retained.
findings.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:563-567 (attestation fields; 'Chain message ... attestations'). [doc] specs/vizor.md:359. [doc] identity.md:271-275 (never on chain; tx bytes retained forever), identity.md:589-593 (24 h deletion duty). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:139 'No X content on chain'.
findings.failure_scenario: A delegate later deletes their X account or asks for their X data to be removed. Their numeric X id and handle remain in vote-chain blocks forever, linked to their public routes. That breaks the X Developer Policy deletion duty and the delegate's privacy expectations, and it cannot be fixed without rewriting chain history.
findings.proposed_fix: Make identity §3.2 `ProxyDelegateRegister{dik_pk, drk_pk, provider, subject_commit, attestation{kind, attestation_id, not_before, expires_at, signatures}, dik_sig, drk_sig}` the only on-chain shape. The verifier's display fields stay in the off-chain attestation response and the directory. Rewrite client §4.3 and Vizor DG-6 to match. Add a chain test asserting that the register message has no string or free-form identity fields.

verdict.reasoning: The stale shapes are real. Client §4.3 sends `MsgRegisterDelegate{dk_pubkey, attestations, pop_sig}`, where the attestations carry provider_user_id, provider_handle and proof_locator. Vizor DG-6 puts `x_user_id` into the chain message. However, the integrated doc (§4.2 and §6), the identity spec (§3.1-3.2) and the chain spec (§4.4, opaque `identity_commitment` only) all agree that only a salted commit goes on chain. In the chain spec's proto there is no field that could carry an X id. The likelier outcome is a decode or integration failure, not X ids written into blocks. That makes this a stale-spec contract mismatch rather than a high privacy hole. It does still need fixing before the client and Vizor build the registration path.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:557-569 (statement and attestation fields; the chain message carries `attestations`). [doc] specs/vizor.md:359. [doc] specs/identity.md:271-275 (never on chain; tx bytes are retained forever), :300-303 (ProxyDelegateRegister has subject_commit only). [doc] specs/chain.md:199-207 (MsgRegisterDelegate has `identity_commitment` only). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:139, :194.
verdict.refined_fix: Make identity §3.2 `ProxyDelegateRegister` the only on-chain shape. Rewrite client §4.3 and Vizor DG-6 so that attestation display fields (handle, user id, locator) live only in the off-chain verifier response and the directory. Add a golden-vector test that the register message has no string fields apart from the verifier ids.

findings.title: The integrated doc overrides in one-liners while component specs stay 'authoritative for detail', so wire contracts diverge everywhere
findings.description:
The integrated doc changes tags, fields, keys and digests with one-line overrides. Every component spec still describes its own superseded choice in full, and no single contract artifact exists. Divergences that would make every proxy tx fail:
- **Tags.** Integrated: 0x09 batch with optional registration, 0x0B registry, 0x0C route. Chain spec: 0x09 batch, 0x0B delegate-and-vote composite, 0x0C register, 0x0F route, 0x10 update. spec_rollout: route 0x0C.
- **DC action fields.** Chain has `delegate_index_bound` but no slot nf and no hint. Circuits has the slot nf and per-action round and anchor. Client has the hint but no slot nf. spec_rollout has none of the three and names the signature `spend_auth_sig`.
- **JSON names for the DC.** `proxy_delegation_commitment` (chain), `proxy_commitment` (client, with `deny_unknown_fields`), `delegation_commitment` (circuits, spec_rollout).
- **REST POST paths.** `/register-delegate` and `/delegate-route` (chain), `/delegate-register` and `/delegate-route-batch` (client), `/proxy-delegate-registry` (identity).
- **FRB DTOs and NextStepKind names.** These differ between client §8 and Vizor §7.3/7.4: `AdvanceProxyBatch` vs `advanceProxyDelegation`, `slot_index` vs `dcIndex`, and differing `ProxyAvailabilityView` enums.
- **Integrated internal inconsistency.** §2 step 3 says 'then 0..50 ZKP2 casts', but §4.1 caps a message at 50 actions in total.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:3 and :97-102. [doc] chain.md:50-56, :94-101, :389-393. [doc] circuits.md:320-329. [doc] client.md:283-288, :567, :584. [doc] spec_rollout.md:176-187, :236. [doc] identity.md:278, :416. [doc] vizor.md:582-597, :629-632. [code] chain REST uses strict canonical JSON (`decodeAndValidateCanonicalJSON`, chain.md:388); client wire structs use `deny_unknown_fields` (client.md:283).
findings.failure_scenario: The chain team implements chain.md and the client team implements client.md. Every 0x09 POST is rejected for an unknown or missing field, or decodes under the wrong tag. Nothing is lost, because no VAN is spent, but integration slips, and each team 'fixes' it locally in a different way.

verdict.reasoning: I checked the sampled divergences and they hold. The chain spec uses 0x0B for the composite, 0x0C register, 0x0F route and 0x10 update; integrated uses 0x0B registry and 0x0C route; spec_rollout proposes route 0x0C. The chain's ProxyDelegationAction has `delegate_index_bound` but no slot nf and no recovery_hint. The ZIP-PD action has neither and names its signature `spend_auth_sig`. Client wire uses `proxy_commitment` with deny_unknown_fields, while chain uses `proxy_delegation_commitment`. The integrated doc says component specs stay 'authoritative for detail unless this doc overrides them', but its overrides are one-liners, so each team will build its own spec. Nothing is lost, because a rejected batch spends no VAN, but integration will fail. This is the umbrella for CMP-5, -6, -7, -8, -12, -13, -14 and -15, which should be tracked as sub-items, not as independent design flaws. The internal 0..50 vs 50-total inconsistency is minor.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/chain.md:49-55 (tag table), :93-101 (action fields). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:176-187 (DelegationCommitmentAction, spend_auth_sig), :236 (route 0x0C). [doc] specs/client.md:282-288 (`proxy_commitment`, deny_unknown_fields). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:3, :31, :92-107.
verdict.refined_fix: Before any implementation PR, publish one contracts-v1 artifact owned by the chain lead. It should hold the proto, JSON names, the tag table, REST paths, digests, KV keys, capability fields, the error table and the FRB DTOs, with Go and Rust golden vectors checked in CI. Mark each overridden section of the component specs 'superseded by contracts-v1 §X'. Fix integrated §2 step 3: the 50-action total includes DCs, and overflow casts go in a follow-up 0x06 against a real anchor.

findings.title: The DIK/DRK key-phrase choice (O4) is not propagated, and Vizor still blocks hardware users and uses a derivation the client spec forbids
findings.description:
The integrated doc picks two Ed25519 keys from a dedicated 24-word phrase, but no other component spec follows it.
- **Chain.** Single DK, MsgRegisterDelegate and MsgUpdateDelegate with rotate/recover/retire, a 48 h recovery delay, a 600 s change interval, and statuses ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/RETIRED.
- **Client.** Single DK from ZIP-32 registered derivation, or random plus backup. `delegate_keys.origin` is in {zip32_registered_v1, random_v1}.
- **Vizor.** Single DK from the account seed via `zip32::arbitrary`, software accounts only (DG-12), DG-2 copy 'comes from this account's recovery phrase', and a recovery scan of identity_index 0..9.
- **spec_rollout ZIP-DR.** Single DK, and `MsgUpdateDelegate{rotate|revoke}`.

The client spec explicitly forbids shipping ad-hoc derivation.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:111-119, :190, :261. [doc] chain.md:194-259, :416-426. [doc] client.md:518-538, :388. [doc] vizor.md:16, :305-307, :320-323, :610-622, :776. [doc] spec_rollout.md:299-319. [doc] client.md:532 'Never ship ad-hoc derivation'.
findings.failure_scenario: Vizor ships DG-2 with seed-derived single keys and blocks Keystone and Ledger users, while the chain implements the DIK/DRK registry. The bridge APIs (`delegate_build_registration(mnemonic, ...)`) cannot produce the dual-key PoP, so registration fails. Any keys already issued from `zip32::arbitrary` would later need a migration.

verdict.reasoning: Integrated O4 picks a dedicated phrase that derives the DIK and DRK, but no component spec follows it. The chain spec has a single DK with MsgUpdateDelegate rotate/recover/retire, a 48 h recovery delay and statuses ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/RETIRED. The client spec uses ZIP-32 registered derivation or random+backup for a single DK. Vizor derives a single DK from the account seed with `zip32::arbitrary`, which the client spec explicitly forbids. Vizor also blocks hardware accounts (DG-12/G8), and its bridge signatures take `mnemonic`, so they cannot produce the dual-key PoP. This is a concrete sub-item of CMP-4 with real rework cost, and keys already issued from seed derivation would need a migration.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:111-119, :191, :260. [doc] specs/chain.md:194-259 (single DK, MsgUpdateDelegate). [doc] specs/client.md:518-538 (registered derivation; 'Never ship ad-hoc derivation'). [doc] specs/vizor.md:16 (software only, seed-derived), :51 (G8), :306 (DG-12), :608-616 (bridge APIs take mnemonic), :615 (`zip32::arbitrary`).
verdict.refined_fix: Declare identity §1-§3 normative for keys and registry. Rewrite chain §4.4-4.6 and §5.1 to use ProxyDelegateEntry with DIK and DRK, and drop the 600 s and 48 h single-DK rules. Rewrite the client §4 key model as phrase-derived keys held in app-level secure storage, not per account. Rewrite Vizor §4.1-4.5 as a phrase create/confirm flow, remove DG-12, and recover by deriving the phrase generations and calling by-key. Record in integrated §0 that the seed-derived and software-only options are rejected.

findings.title: Four incompatible route digests and two digest conventions for registry signatures
findings.evidence: [doc] chain.md:336-359. [doc] identity.md:185-203. [doc] client.md:577, :566. [doc] spec_rollout.md:245, :306-312.
findings.failure_scenario:
There are two ways this fails:
- **Mismatch.** If the Vizor route signer and the chain verifier disagree on a single byte, every route is rejected. All pools abstain on every proposal, so delegated weight has no effect on the tally (decision 2 permits no fallback).
- **Replay.** If the identity convention is used without a chain id, a stage chain and a mainnet vote chain both on Zcash network 'main' can produce the same round_id (ea_pk is not in the preimage, chain.md:646). A route signed on one chain can then be replayed on the other when index, epoch and DRK match. [inference]
findings.proposed_fix: Use one convention everywhere: BLAKE2b-256, an ASCII domain, then `lp8(chain_id)`, then the `write32`/`writeU32As32`/`writeU64As32` idiom from sighash.go, with key_epoch as u64. Take identity's field sets (DIK, DRK, subject_commit, attestation_id). The route digest is `SVOTE_PROXY_DELEGATE_ROUTE_V1 || lp8(chain_id) || round_id || u32 index || u64 key_epoch || u32 n || (u32 p, u32 decision)*`, signed by the DRK. Generate vectors from the `zcash_vote_delegate` crate and mirror them in Go and e2e sighash.rs before implementation starts.

verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/chain.md:336-359 (D3-D7 with lp8(chain_id)). [doc] specs/identity.md:75, :185-203 (the route row has no `net`; the others use u32 key_epoch and LE). [doc] specs/client.md:577. [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:245. [code] x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:401-413 (deriveRoundID inputs).
verdict.refined_fix: Adopt the chain D-convention everywhere: BLAKE2b-256, ASCII domain, lp8(chain_id), the write32/writeU32As32/writeU64As32 helpers, and key_epoch as u64. Use identity's field sets (DIK, DRK, subject_commit, attestation_id). Route digest: `SVOTE_PROXY_DELEGATE_ROUTE_V1 || lp8(chain_id) || round_id || index || key_epoch || n || (p, decision)*`, signed by the DRK. Generate golden vectors from the shared `zcash_vote_delegate` crate and mirror them in Go and e2e sighash.rs.

findings.title: KV layout contradictions and missing backing stores (PoolShareCount, the proxy-actions feed, IAVL route keys)
findings.description:
The KV layouts conflict:
- **chain spec:** 0x1A record, 0x1B key index, 0x1C route set, 0x1D params, 0x1E next index, 0x1F routing base;
- **integrated and identity:** a 0x1A sub-family with params inside it, routes at 0x1B, routing base at 0x1C, and **another** params key at 0x1D.

Several stores are named but never defined:
- **PoolShareCount** (integrated §4.1) has no prefix, no genesis entry and no IAVL key.
- **Slot nullifier set 0x03** needs a NullifierType constant and genesis export.
- **Route keys.** Vizor §7.9 plans IAVL proofs for a per-proposal `DelegateRoute{round,d,p}` key that does not exist; routes are stored as one set per (round, d).
- **proxy-actions feed** (integrated §4.2, client R1/R2) has no backing state. Today nullifier values are just `[]byte{1}`, so the client's `GET /nullifier/{round}/gov/{nf} -> {tx_hash, height}` cannot be answered from state. Node indexer settings vary: one script sets `indexer = "null"`.
findings.evidence: [doc] chain.md:403-413. [doc] identity.md:384-392. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:131, :139-140, :149. [doc] vizor.md:703. [doc] client.md:475, :483. [code] x/vote/types/keys.go:113 (nullifier value `[]byte{1}`), keys.go:98-107 (types 0x00-0x02 only), keys.go:114-207 (0x1A+ unused). [code] scripts/reset-snapshot.sh:76.
findings.failure_scenario: R2 recovery (UFVK only), which the integrated doc promises, has no feed to scan, so a reinstalled delegator can neither find its DCs nor redeliver their shares. Separately, Vizor's 'Verified' badge for routes is built against a key that is never written, so verification always fails.

verdict.reasoning:
The KV layouts do conflict: chain uses 0x1A-0x1F as separate records, while integrated and identity use a 0x1A sub-family plus 0x1B/0x1C/0x1D, so verifier sets and params may be stored twice. Two parts of the finding are overstated.
- **PoolShareCount.** It can simply reuse ShareCountKey(round,0,d), as the chain spec does. VoteSummary iterates only round.Proposals (ids >= 1), so proposal 0 never reaches it.
- **Proxy-actions feed.** The feed is not impossible without state. DC bytes and the `vote_action_batch` event, including its leaf indices, sit in blocks and block results, which can be scanned without the tx indexer. Still, no design names a source for the feed that R1/R2 depend on, and that gap is real.
- **Vizor route keys.** Vizor's per-(round,d,p) IAVL route key does not exist. The result is an 'Unverified' label, not lost weight.

[code] x/vote/types/keys.go:101-114 (types 0x00-0x02; value []byte{1}). [code] x/vote/keeper/keeper_tally.go:196-199 (VoteSummary iterates round.Proposals only).

findings.title: ZKP4 public inputs, FFI packing and DC-secret PRF still differ across circuits, chain and ZIP-PD
findings.evidence: [doc] circuits.md:73-86, :453-458, :467. [doc] chain.md:731-740. [doc] spec_rollout.md:141-155, :172. [doc] client.md:233-241. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:63-64, :71. [inference] A DeliverTx failure leaves the tx bytes, including the ciphertexts, in the block. Reusing r_i for a different v_i then publishes `C2 - C2' = (v-v')G`, and that difference is small enough for BSGS.
findings.failure_scenario: A third-party wallet follows the ZIP-PD text (no slot nf, PRF without (d, w)). Its proofs fail on chain. If it retries after a DeliverTx failure with a changed amount, the share-value differences become public.
findings.proposed_fix: Freeze integrated §3's 11-PI order, plus the bound as PI 11 only if O1 fits. The chain FFI builds instances with voting-circuits' `Instance::to_halo2_instance`, and the buffer length is NUM_PUBLIC_INPUTS x 32. Rewrite ZIP-PD §1.4.4 to match. Implement the client's dc_seed PRF in voting-circuits and change the circuits §8.1-8.2 builder to take `dc_seed`, not `sk`. Delete spec_rollout's PRF text.

verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/circuits.md:68-86 (11 PIs), :451-458 (PRF keyed by sk, binds d and w), :467 (FFI 352). [doc] specs/chain.md:731-740 (288-byte packing, bound at 7). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:141-155, :164, :172 (PRF context without d and w). [doc] specs/client.md:233-241. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:69-72, :78.
verdict.refined_fix: Freeze integrated §3's PI order, and append the bound as PI 11 only if O1 fits. The chain FFI builds instances through voting-circuits' `Instance` constructor, with one documented packing (compressed points as in ZKP2, or 11x32), pinned by a vector. Rewrite ZIP-PD §1.4.4 to match, delete its PRF text, and point to the dc_seed PRF implemented in voting-circuits. Change the circuits §8.1-8.2 builders to take dc_seed instead of sk.

findings.title: ZIP-PD text reverses the on-chain leaf append order
findings.description: spec_rollout §1.4.5 (the normative ZIP-PD text) says the appended leaves are 'DC leaves in action order, then VC leaves, then the final VAN'. The code, the chain spec, the client spec and the integrated doc all append the final VAN first, then the commitments in action order. Third-party wallets implementing ZIP-PD would compute every DC tree_position off by one.
findings.evidence: [code] x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:250-262: the final VAN is appended, then each commitment. [doc] spec_rollout.md:200. [doc] chain.md:143. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:108. [doc] client.md:457.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-Vizor wallet builds DC share payloads with the ZIP's positions. The helper's `vcHash == leaf[tree_position]` check (internal/helper/api.go:663-679) fails. The shares are rejected, and the DC's weight never reaches Pool[d] (lost for that round).
findings.proposed_fix: Fix ZIP-PD to 'final successor VAN, then each action commitment in action order', matching the code. Require wallets to take leaf indices from the `vote_action_batch` event. Add a cross-implementation vector to e2e.

verdict.reasoning: The ZIP-PD text says 'DC leaves, then VC leaves, then the final VAN'. The code appends the final VAN first, then each commitment, and the chain, client and integrated docs all agree with the code. The defect is real but is confined to a draft ZIP. Both the chain spec and ZIP-PD emit leaf indices in the batch event, so a wallet that reads the event gets correct positions even under the wrong prose. That makes it an erratum, not a design change.
verdict.evidence: [code] x/vote/keeper/msg_server.go:252-265 (AppendCommitment(final VAN), then each VoteCommitment). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:200 (wrong order), :202 (event carries dc/vc/final leaf indices). [doc] specs/chain.md:143-147. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:108. [code] internal/helper/api.go:663-677 (leaf check at tree_position).
verdict.refined_fix: Correct ZIP-PD §1.4.5 to 'final successor VAN, then each action commitment in action order'. Make it normative that wallets take positions from the `vote_action_batch` event. Add a cross-implementation leaf-order vector to e2e.

findings.title: The client never allocates or persists dc_slot, and Vizor's 'Delegate more' contradicts the client's single locked allocation
findings.description:
The integrated doc adopts the circuit slot nullifier (C14, set 0x03, `dc_slot_nf` in the action and the sighash). The client spec, which is authoritative for client detail, never mentions dc_slot or a slot nullifier. Its `proxy_slots.slot_index` is a per-bundle 0..9 planner index, unrelated to the circuit's per-registration-chain 0..15 slot.

Vizor §3.7 ships 'Delegate more', a second batch from the successor VAN. The client schema allows one allocation per (round, wallet), refuses `clear` after reservation, and lists top-ups as 'not in v1'.
findings.evidence: [doc] grep for dc_slot, slot_nullifier and slot_nf finds no hits in client.md or vizor.md. [doc] client.md:351 (PK round_id, wallet_id), :365 (slot_index 0..9), :375, :512. [doc] client.summary.md:46 (open question 4). [doc] vizor.md:249, :442. [doc] circuits.md:163, :577 (C1: allocate slots sequentially, recover via dc_slot_nullifier).
findings.failure_scenario: The user delegates to 3 delegates, then uses 'Delegate more' for 2 more. If the client reuses slot_index 0 and 1 as the circuit slot, the second batch's slot nullifiers duplicate set 0x03 entries and the chain rejects the tx. If the first allocation is locked, the SDK refuses the request outright. Either way the Vizor screen built for this flow cannot complete.

verdict.reasoning: Integrated adopts C14: slot nullifiers in set 0x03, carried in the action and the sighash. The client spec has no dc_slot or slot nullifier anywhere. Its `proxy_slots.slot_index` (0..9 per bundle) is a planner index. Circuits requires slots to be allocated sequentially per registration chain, because rand is shared across successor VANs, and recovered through slot-nf queries. Vizor §3.7 ships 'Delegate more' as a second batch from the successor VAN. The client schema makes the allocation PK (round, wallet), locks it, and recommends no top-ups in v1. The flow cannot complete as specified.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:351 (PK round_id, wallet_id), :365 (slot_index 0..9), :376 (UNIQUE bundle, delegate). [doc] specs/client.summary.md:46 (q4: not in v1). [doc] specs/vizor.md:249, :442. [doc] specs/circuits.md:163-166 (C14 shares nk, round and rand per chain), :577 (C1 sequential slots). A grep for dc_slot, slot_nf or slot nullifier finds nothing in client.md or vizor.md.
verdict.refined_fix: For v1, keep one locked allocation per round and remove Vizor's 'Delegate more' state, CTA and copy. In client schema v25, add `dc_slot` (0..15, unique per round, wallet and bundle chain) and `dc_slot_nullifier`, and persist both before proving. In recovery, probe nullifier type 0x03 for s in 0..15. Carry the slot nf in the wire and the sighash. If top-ups come later, add a per-chain slot cursor.

findings.title: Five incompatible late-delegation policies, and the integrated §4.4 contradicts itself
findings.description:
The policies:
- **Integrated:** 'same last-moment logic as votes' (single-share DCs) and also 'blocks new delegation inside the helper last-moment buffer, with a hard cutoff 30 min before end'.
- **Chain spec:** a stored cutoff, `end - clamp(10%, 60 s, 1 h)`.
- **Client:** allows DCs in the last-moment window with the single-share layout.
- **Vizor:** blocks only at end - 10 min, with a 24 h warning.
- **spec_rollout:** MUST NOT start after end - 30 min.

Single-share DCs expose the exact amount to an EA-threshold coalition, and late DCs risk shares that are not revealed in time.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:32, :163. [doc] chain.md:18, :77-83, :584. [doc] client.md:215. [doc] vizor.md:167-168, :288. [doc] spec_rollout.md:291-294.
findings.failure_scenario: Vizor lets a user delegate at end - 15 min with the single-share layout. Either the SDK refuses because it follows the integrated rule (a confusing error after the review screen), or it sends the DC and the share misses vote_end_time because the helper has a 5-minute retry cutoff. Either way the weight is lost, and the copy promised it would be counted.
findings.proposed_fix: One rule, owned by the client and mirrored in Vizor: refuse new proxy batches once `now >= vote_end_time - max(last_moment_buffer, 30 min)`. Remove the single-share DC layout entirely: layout 1, PRF domain 0x14 and the hint layout byte. Keep no chain cutoff. Vizor copy shows the exact cutoff time, with a 24 h warning.

verdict.reasoning: There are five policies. Integrated §4.4 says both 'same last-moment logic as votes', which today means single-share, and 'blocks new delegation inside the last-moment buffer plus a 30 min cutoff', while §2 step 4 still describes single-share DCs. The chain stores a cutoff; the client uses single-share in the window; Vizor blocks at end-10 min; ZIP-PD blocks at end-30 min. Note that the SDK's buffer is 40% of the round, capped at 6 h. A 'block inside the buffer' rule therefore closes delegation up to 6 h before end, which the owner and the copy must reflect. If the SDK enforces its own rule, the mismatch causes a late, confusing refusal. Weight is lost only if a DC lands and its shares miss vote_end.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:32, :163, :259. [doc] specs/chain.md:122 (cutoff_time in ante). [doc] specs/client.md:215 (single-share in the window), :703. [doc] specs/vizor.md:167-168. [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:291-294. [code] zcash_voting/src/share_policy/timing.rs:20-24, :32-44 (buffer = 40% of duration, capped at 6 h).
verdict.refined_fix: Use one client-owned rule, mirrored in Vizor: refuse to plan **or broadcast** a new proxy batch once `now >= vote_end - max(last_moment_buffer, 30 min)`. A refused broadcast spends no VAN. Remove the single-share DC layout (layout 1, PRF domain 0x14, hint layout byte) and keep no chain cutoff. Vizor shows the exact cutoff time with a 24 h warning, and the owner is told that delegation can close up to 6 h before voting ends.
