findings.title: Directory, static-config and snapshot formats are specified four ways, and per-round pinning is both required and rejected
findings.failure_scenario: The static config is sha256-pinned in the app binary. If it ships with the wrong section, Vizor needs a new pin and an app-store release before the directory works. A Vizor that accepts a 7-day-old profiles document also violates the X keep-current rule that identity is designed around.
findings.proposed_fix: Adopt identity §5 as normative: index, registry, profiles and avatars; online and offline directory keys; a 30 h profiles expiry; seq plus equivocation checks. Use one static section name, `proxy_delegation`. Do not pin a snapshot per round, and rewrite spec_rollout T11 to rely on the chain overlay plus the seq hash chain. Update client §5.2 and Vizor §7.8.

verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:613-621, :683. [doc] specs/identity.md:584-588 (30 h expiry), :677 (no per-round pin). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:282, :286. [doc] specs/vizor.md:679-682 (7-day window), :52 (G6 delegate_registry).
verdict.refined_fix: Make identity §5 normative: index, registry, profiles and avatars; online and offline directory keys; a 30 h profiles expiry; seq plus equivocation checks. Use one static section, `proxy_delegation`. Drop `registry_snapshot_sha256` from the per-round extension, and rewrite spec_rollout T11 to rely on the chain overlay plus the seq hash chain. Update client §5.2 and Vizor §7.8 so they purge expired profiles, keeping index and fingerprint data.

findings.title: Avatar formats are incompatible, so the 'profile picture' requirement fails silently, and Vizor decodes with platform codecs
findings.description:
The three specs disagree:
- **identity:** emits re-encoded **WebP** at exactly 64 or 256 px, decoded in Rust with `image-webp` and handed to Dart as pixels.
- **Vizor:** validates 'PNG magic, at most 64 KB, `instantiateImageCodec` dimensions at most 256x256'. `instantiateImageCodec` is a platform codec parsing network bytes, which contradicts the integrated rule 'Images decoded in Rust'.
- **client:** accepts PNG or WebP up to 256 KiB and 512 px.

The review policies conflict too. Vizor shows identicons until **every** picture is human-approved. Identity sends only featured delegates to review.
findings.evidence: [doc] identity.md:715-726, :733. [doc] vizor.md:686-692, :822. [doc] client.md:640-641. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:211.
findings.failure_scenario: Every WebP fails Vizor's PNG-magic check and falls back to an identicon, so the ICNS-style 'search influencers with profile picture' experience ships without pictures. Alternatively, if PNG is used, platform decoders parse attacker-influenced bytes, which is the libwebp/BLASTPASS class identity was designed to avoid.
findings.proposed_fix: Use WebP only, at exactly 64 or 256 px, verify the sha256 against the profiles doc, decode with Rust `image-webp`, and render with `decodeImageFromPixels`. Delete Vizor's PNG and `instantiateImageCodec` path, and add a test banning it. The owner decides the review policy. Recommendation: auto-approve non-featured pictures after the CSAM and pHash checks, and send featured ones to human review.

verdict.reasoning: Identity emits re-encoded WebP at exactly 64 or 256 px and decodes it in Rust, passing pixels to Dart. Vizor checks for PNG magic, caps at 64 KB and calls `instantiateImageCodec` before drawing with `Image.memory`. Both of those run platform codecs on network bytes, which contradicts integrated §7. The client accepts PNG or WebP up to 256 KiB and 512 px. If Vizor follows its own spec, every WebP fails the PNG check and falls back to an identicon. The review policies also conflict: Vizor shows nothing until every picture is approved, while identity sends only featured delegates to human review. Integrated §6 and §7 already imply the WebP plus Rust-decode answer, but the Vizor and client specs still describe the opposite.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/identity.md:715-726. [doc] specs/vizor.md:686-692, :819-822. [doc] specs/client.md:640-642. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:195, :211.
verdict.refined_fix: Use WebP only, at exactly 64 or 256 px. Verify the sha256 against the profiles doc, decode in Rust with `image-webp`, and render with `decodeImageFromPixels`. Delete the PNG, `instantiateImageCodec` and `Image.memory` paths from the Vizor and client specs, and extend Vizor's grep test to ban them. List the review policy (featured-only human review vs. every picture) as an owner decision.

findings.title: Four fingerprint definitions and four deep-link formats for a link that becomes permanent once shared
findings.evidence: [doc] client.md:543. [doc] identity.md:78-83, :981. [doc] spec_rollout.md:301, :481. [doc] vizor.md:110, :718-719. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:210. [code] vizor-deeplink-server README:88-90 (no wildcards, per the vizor spec).
findings.failure_scenario: Influencers share links during the beta. A later change of format or fingerprint makes those links show 'key mismatch' banners, or fail to resolve.
findings.proposed_fix: Fingerprint the DIK as the first 16 data characters of its `zvdk1` bech32m string. Users can compare it by eye against the X post, it is 80-bit, and no hash is needed. Use the link `https://link.vizor.cash/d/<index>#k=<16 chars>`. The wallet resolves by index from the chain and requires the prefix to match. Freeze this in contracts-v1 before the beta.

verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:543. [doc] specs/identity.md:78-83, :981. [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:301, :481, :510 ('after the link format freezes'). [doc] specs/vizor.md:73, :370. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:210.
verdict.refined_fix: In contracts-v1, before the beta, freeze one fingerprint (identity's 60-bit BLAKE2b with its test vector, or the 16-char zvdk1 data prefix) and one link format, `https://link.vizor.cash/d/<index>#k=<fp>`. The wallet resolves by index from the chain and treats the fingerprint as a hint. Add the deeplink server's single regex route.

findings.title: The privacy claim 'DC target is unlinkable at tx time' is false while the immediate share applies to DC shares
findings.description: Integrated §8 says which delegate a DC targets is 'revealed only per share at helper-randomized times, unlinkable to the DC'. The SDK designates one immediate share per round. In proxy-only rounds the client makes it a DC share (open owner question 2), and single-share last-moment DCs also reveal at once. In both cases a `reveal_pool_share(d)` follows the proxy tx within seconds.
findings.evidence: [code] zcash_voting src/share_policy/initial_placement.rs:30-39 (`round_immediate_share_key`). [doc] client.md:336-337, :705. [doc] client.summary.md:44. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:221.
findings.failure_scenario: An observer correlates each anonymous proxy-only tx with the pool reveal that lands right after it. That reveals which delegate the tx chose, and with the public reveal count, a rough size class. The privacy section given to the owner overstates the protection.
findings.proposed_fix: The owner decides; the recommendation is never to designate a DC share as immediate. In proxy-only rounds the progress step completes on helper acknowledgement of all shares, not on an on-chain reveal. Correct §8 to say that helpers learn d, and that any immediate or single-share DC is linkable by timing.

verdict.reasoning: Integrated §8 claims that the DC target is 'unlinkable to the DC'. The client spec itself says reveals are unlinkable 'except through the immediate share'. In proxy-only rounds, the client recommends designating a DC share as immediate (owner q2). Late DCs use the single-share layout. In both cases a `(0, d)` reveal follows the anonymous proxy tx within seconds, which links the tx to d by timing for any chain observer. The privacy section as given to the owner overstates the protection.
verdict.evidence: [code] zcash_voting/src/share_policy/initial_placement.rs:23, :30-39 (round_immediate_share_key). [doc] specs/client.md:335-337 (proxy-only immediate share = slot 0, share 0), :215 (single-share when late), :703-705 ('unlinkable to the tx except through the immediate share'). [doc] specs/client.summary.md:44. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:221.
verdict.refined_fix: Recommend to the owner that a DC share is never immediate: proxy-only rounds show 'sent' on helper acknowledgement, not on an on-chain reveal. Late single-share DCs disappear if CMP-11 is adopted. Correct §8 to say that helpers learn d, and that any immediate or single-share DC reveal is linkable to its tx by timing.

findings.title: The 'Abstain option' mitigation makes leak (a) worse, and coexists with an uncounted abstain sentinel
findings.description:
§8 offers an explicit Abstain **option** on every proposal as the mitigation for differencing leak (b). An Abstain option is usually thinly used by direct voters, so a delegate routing Abstain is likely the **sole contributor** to that bucket. Its exact Pool[d] is then decrypted and published, which is leak (a).

The 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel ('recorded, not counted') is kept alongside it, so delegates who use the sentinel still enable differencing. Adding an option also changes the ballot that Zodl voters see.
findings.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:124, :228-232, :261. [doc] spec_rollout.md:382-391. [doc] chain.md:32. [doc] vizor.md:224-225. [inference] In NU7-style polls, few direct voters choose a neutral option.
findings.failure_scenario: Following the nudge, a delegate routes Abstain on proposal 3. No direct voter or other delegate picks Abstain. The published total for (3, Abstain) equals Pool[d] exactly, which violates decision 4 and exposes small delegators when the pool has a single delegator.
findings.proposed_fix:
Present this to the owner as a trade-off, not as a mitigation. Either:
- (A) no Abstain option: keep the sentinel and disclose differencing; or
- (B) an Abstain option: drop the sentinel from the client UI (map 'Abstain' to the option), and warn in DG-10 that routing to a rarely used option can reveal the pool total.

In both cases, state in §8 that decision 4 cannot be fully honored for delegates who abstain or skip proposals.

verdict.reasoning: An explicit Abstain option lets delegates route every proposal, which does cancel turnout differencing (leak b). It also creates a bucket that direct voters rarely use. A delegate routing Abstain is then likely the sole contributor, and the decrypted (p, Abstain) total equals Pool[d] exactly (leak a) [inference]. The 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel is still allowed, so delegates who use it re-enable differencing. Presenting the option as a mitigation without the trade-off misleads the owner about decision 4.
verdict.evidence: [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:125 (sentinel kept), :229-232 (leaks and the mitigation), :261 (O5). [doc] specs/spec_rollout.summary.md (open question recommending the Abstain option). [doc] specs/vizor.md:224-225.
verdict.refined_fix: Rewrite §8 as an owner trade-off. (A) No Abstain option: keep the sentinel and disclose differencing. (B) An Abstain option: drop the sentinel from the client (UI 'Abstain' maps to the option), and warn delegates in DG-10 that routing to a thinly used option can reveal their pool total. In both cases, state that decision 4 cannot be fully honored for delegates who abstain or skip proposals.

findings.title: The recovery promised in the integrated doc is not implemented in Vizor, and the copy claims 'still counts' in a window where weight is lost
findings.description:
The integrated doc adopts R1 and R2 recovery via the recovery hint, the ARK and the proxy-actions feed. Vizor §8 still says that a reinstall loses which delegates were chosen, the amounts and share tracking, and that 'The delegation still counts, because shares were handed to helpers at submission'.

Shares cannot be handed over at submission. Helper payloads need `tree_position`, which is known only after inclusion, and Vizor's own state machine delivers shares after 'confirming'. Vizor has no ARK, feed-scan or redelivery flow, and the feed has no store (CMP-7).
findings.evidence: [code] zcash_voting src/share.rs:1026, :1091 (payloads use `vc_tree_position`). [doc] vizor.md:502, :776, :780, :796. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:176. [doc] client.md:467-498, :773-776.
findings.failure_scenario:
There are two failures:
- **Weight lost.** A user confirms delegating 40 ZEC, the DC lands, and the app is deleted or crashes before share delivery. No shares ever reach the helpers, and the DC weight is lost even though the UI promised it 'still counts'.
- **Unused recovery.** With R2 available in the SDK but not wired into Vizor, the user never runs it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Vizor work item: on account restore, derive the ARK from the UFVK, scan `/proxy-actions/{round}`, show the recovered delegations and verification, and redeliver missing shares. Fix copy C8 to 'If you reinstall before your delegation is sent to helpers, open Vizor again before voting ends so it can finish.' Back the feed with the 0x1E store from CMP-7.

verdict.reasoning: Vizor §8 says 'the delegation still counts, because shares were handed to helpers at submission'. Vizor's own state machine contradicts this: deliveringShares runs only after 'confirming --included + leaf positions'. The SDK also builds helper payloads with `vc_tree_position`, which is known only after inclusion. Vizor plans no ARK, feed-scan or redelivery flow, so the R2 recovery that integrated promises has no UI. One part is overstated: a crash keeps the DB and resumes through R0. Only uninstall or restore between broadcast and share delivery loses the weight, which is a narrow window and the same as for votes today.

findings.title: Per-index registry lookups by delegators leak their chosen delegates to the vote server
findings.evidence: [doc] client.md:625-626. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:182. [doc] vizor.md:710. [doc] identity.md:666-667. [doc] spec_rollout.md:355 (Tor opt-in and off by default).
findings.failure_scenario: A vote-server operator logs `/delegates/17` and `/delegates/203` from IP X, followed by a 2-DC proxy tx from X a minute later. That links the delegator's IP to their choices, which T2 claims are hidden from everyone except helpers.
findings.proposed_fix: Delegators sync the whole registry (paged, using `updated_since_height`) and never call `/delegates/{d}`. Chain cross-checks use IAVL proofs for a fixed-size set of 10 keys (the chosen delegates plus random decoys), fetched in a single batch through the Tor-aware client at each check. Add a test asserting that no per-index REST call happens in delegator flows.

verdict.reasoning: The client calls `resolve(d)`, which fetches `/delegates/{d}`, at preview, at commit and before proving. Integrated does IAVL proofs of the selected records at the same points, and Vizor adds 3 decoys. Identity says delegators must never query per index, and Tor is off by default. The RPC operator sees the IP plus the queried indices and then a proxy tx from the same IP, which defeats the claim that the choice is hidden at tx time. Any per-key IAVL proof discloses the key. The proposed decoy fix also has a flaw: if decoys are redrawn at each of the three checks, intersecting the queried sets reveals the real choices.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/client.md:625-627. [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:182. [doc] specs/vizor.md:703-710 (3 decoys per batch). [doc] specs/identity.md:414-415 (by-key for delegate tooling only; delegators page the whole list), :666-667. [doc] specs/spec_rollout.md:355 (Tor opt-in).
verdict.refined_fix: Delegators sync the whole registry, paged with `updated_since_height`, and never call `/delegates/{d}`. For IAVL cross-checks, choose one fixed decoy set per allocation (chosen plus random up to 10 keys), persist it, and query exactly that set in one batch at every check, so intersection reveals nothing. Add a test that delegator flows make no per-index REST call.

findings.title: No scheduled legal or compliance review, and the X ToS change lands in four days
findings.evidence: [doc] identity.md:594, :731, :483. [doc] identity.summary.md:51. [doc] spec_rollout.md:426-435. Today is 2026-10-05.

Identity notes that X ToS changes take effect 2026-10-09 and that redistribution needs legal review, and its CSAM pipeline implies a reporting duty. The 'four days' urgency is misleading, though. The verifier is built from week 3, so the review only has to cover the terms in force when it ships. Losing X access does not touch registered entries, routes or weight; it blocks new X registrations and profile hydration, and GitHub and DNS ship at launch as fallbacks.

findings.title: App-store UGC plan conflicts: report via external web form vs in-app, and no text moderation
findings.description:
Identity §7.5 routes reports to an external browser form ('no in-app POST'). Vizor §10 builds an in-app POST to functions.vizor.cash. Google Play's UGC policy calls for an in-app reporting system [inference]. Neither spec owns the report backend end to end.

The text limits also differ. Identity statements are up to 500 chars with one URL. Vizor shows bios up to 160 chars with no links and expects a `text_status`, but identity defines no text-moderation state. App Privacy labels, reviewer access to a live proxy round, and a demo delegate are not planned.
findings.evidence: [doc] identity.md:257-260, :810. [doc] vizor.md:815-833. [doc] spec_rollout.md:837 (checklist line only).
findings.failure_scenario: Play or App Store review rejects the build because reporting leaves the app, or because user-authored delegate statements are shown with no moderation state. The Vizor release slips past the planned first proxy round.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an in-app report sheet that POSTs through NetworkHttpClient to a verifier `/v1/reports` endpoint, with no account id. Add `text_state` to the profiles doc, with a moderation queue in the publisher. Use one limit: 280 chars and no links. Update the App Privacy labels. Prepare reviewer notes with a stage build, a demo delegate and an always-open test round.

verdict.reasoning: Identity §7.5 opens an external browser form and states there is no in-app POST. Vizor §10 builds an in-app POST to functions.vizor.cash, an endpoint the identity spec does not define. Vizor gates display name and bio on `text_status == approved` and limits bios to 160 chars with no links. Identity defines no text-moderation state, and its statements allow 500 chars with one URL. Apple 1.2 requires filtering and a report mechanism, and Google Play's UGC policy asks for in-app reporting [inference]. Unmoderated user text, plus reporting that leaves the app, is a credible store-review risk, and no spec owns the report backend end to end.
verdict.evidence: [doc] specs/identity.md:257-260 (500 chars, one URL), :810 (external form, no in-app POST). [doc] specs/vizor.md:98, :815-833 (text_status, 160 chars, in-app POST).
verdict.refined_fix: Use an in-app report sheet that POSTs through NetworkHttpClient to a verifier-owned `/v1/reports` endpoint, with no account id. Add `text_state` and a moderation queue to the identity publisher and profiles doc. Use one text limit (for example 280 chars, no links). Plan App Privacy labels and reviewer notes with a stage build, a demo delegate and an open test round.

findings.title: Operational components are missing: coordinator tooling, per-round enable, chain monitoring, canary and explorer
findings.description:
Five operational pieces are missing:
- **Coordinator tooling.** The coordinator UI (`ui/`, the round generator) only signs MsgCreateVotingSession and MsgUpdateVoteManagers. No tool proposes the new verifier, params or suspension payloads.
- **Per-round enable.** This comes from a global `enable_for_new_rounds` snapshot taken when the create action executes. Running a proxy round and a non-proxy round in the same week therefore means sequencing N-of-M param flips around round-creation actions that have a 7-day TTL.
- **Chain monitoring.** No chain-side monitoring for routing EndBlock duration, `pools_routed`, or reveal rejections with `ErrDelegateNotFound` and permanent helper p=0 errors, which mean burned weight. No registry-op rate.
- **Canary.** No end-to-end canary (a delegator plus a delegate in each round).
- **Explorer.** No explorer or indexer item. The admin UI's VoteSummary shows 0 ballots for options that only pools fed.
findings.evidence: [code] vote-sdk ui/README.md (round builder, MsgCreateVotingSession/MsgUpdateVoteManagers via Keplr). [doc] docs/vote-coordinator-actions.md (threshold approvals, TTL). [doc] chain.md:436, :574. [code] keeper_tally.go:197-209. [doc] identity.md:871-890 (verifier monitoring only).
findings.failure_scenario:
There are three failures:
- **Wrong enable flag.** A production round is created while `enable_for_new_rounds` is still true from a [TEST] round, so proxy is enabled without a signed config extension (this fails safe but is confusing).
- **Silent burn.** A client bug sends DCs to a stale index, and nobody notices the permanent reveal rejections until users complain after the tally.
- **No tooling.** Coordinators cannot suspend an impersonator quickly because no tool builds the payload.
findings.proposed_fix:
Add these work items:
- **Tooling:** svoted CLI and generator-UI support for the new coordinator payloads.
- **Per-round enable:** replace it with `MsgSetRoundProxyDelegation{round_id, enabled}`, valid only before the round becomes ACTIVE and set-once, or document a strict runbook.
- **Metrics and alerts:** Prometheus metrics with bounded labels for routing duration, pool reveals accepted and rejected by reason, and registry ops, with alerts on any p=0 permanent rejection.
- **Canary:** a scripted canary delegate and delegator in every proxy round that asserts `totals == direct + routed`.
- **Explorer:** event docs for third-party explorers.

verdict.reasoning:
The UI already proposes several coordinator payloads, but none for the new proxy params or suspension, and no svoted CLI path is specced. Monitoring for routing EndBlock time, pool reveals rejected by reason, and permanent helper rejections for an unknown d (burned weight) is missing, as are a canary and explorer docs. Two parts of the finding are overstated.
- **Per-round enable** is fail-safe. Vizor also requires a signed per-round extension plus chain capabilities, so a stray chain enable only hides or exposes nothing.
- **Coordinator actions** have a 7-day TTL but are not a blocker.
These are operational work items, not design changes.

findings.title: Status, delay, limit and error vocabularies still differ across specs
findings.description:
The differences:
- **Statuses:** ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/RETIRED (chain) vs ACTIVE/FROZEN/REVOKED plus a `coordinator_suspended` flag (identity, integrated) vs {Active, ProofRemoved, Suspended, KeyChangePending, Retired} (client DTO).
- **Key-recovery delay:** 48 h (chain) vs 7 d (identity, integrated).
- **Attestation validity:** up to 7 d (chain) vs 72 h (integrated, identity param) vs 24 h issued (identity verifier).
- **Registry per-block cap:** 'none needed' (chain) vs enforced in Prepare/ProcessProposal (identity, integrated).
- **Suspension payload:** `MsgSetDelegateStatus` with a free-text reason (chain) vs `MsgSetProxyDelegateSuspension` with reason codes (identity).
- **Error names:** Vizor uses `key_revoked` and `post_not_found`; identity uses `MARKER_MISSING` and `PROOF_NOT_FOUND`; the chain uses codes 50-62.
- **Delegate directory latency:** Vizor copy says 'within about an hour', but identity lists new delegates only after 24 h.
findings.failure_scenario: Vizor maps chain error 53 to the wrong copy, or tells a new delegate that their profile is live in an hour while it stays lookup-only for 24 h. Support load and confusion follow; nothing is lost.

findings.title: Nothing replaces analytics to measure adoption or failure rates
findings.description: Vizor has no telemetry by design. No spec defines how the team will measure adoption, delegator success (k/16 at the end), delegate routing rates or onboarding funnel drop-off. Directly publishing per-delegate counts would undermine the 'no leaderboard' mitigation.
findings.evidence: [doc] vizor.md:243 (never log URLs or keys). [doc] spec_rollout.md:842 ('dashboards live' with no definition). [doc] integrated-design-v1.md:232.
findings.failure_scenario: After the first proxy round the team cannot tell whether a third of delegators ended at 14/16, or how many verifications failed at `MARKER_MISSING`, and so cannot prioritize fixes.
findings.proposed_fix: Build a public aggregate dashboard from chain events: total DCs per round, the share of DCs fully revealed, the share of routed (d, p) pairs, and p=0 rejection counts. It has no per-delegate rows. Add verifier-side funnel metrics (resolve, attest, register) with no personal data. Document both as the analytics substitute.

findings.title: Performance and size assumptions were measured only on a dev workstation, and conflict with the launch gates
findings.description:
Routing measured 1.39 s for 10k delegates x 50 proposals on an M3 Ultra. spec_rollout's load pass criterion is routing EndBlock of at most 500 ms, and identity allows `max_delegates` of 1,000,000. ZKP4 prove time was measured only on a loaded M3 Ultra. Mobile time and memory (ZKP2 and ZKP4 keys together use about 276 MiB peak) are unmeasured.

The JSON size estimates disagree: about 0.94 MB (client) vs a 577 KB raw composite (chain), against a 1 MiB REST LimitReader. The load matrix has no directory CDN case and no verifier onboarding-spike case.
findings.evidence: [doc] chain.md:574. [doc] spec_rollout.md:740. [doc] identity.md:335. [doc] circuits.md:233-237, :249. [doc] client.md:60. [doc] chain.md:171. [code] api/handler.go: `io.LimitReader(r.Body, 1<<20)`.
findings.failure_scenario: On validator-class hardware, routing for a large registry exceeds the launch gate, and the gate is then quietly waived. Or ZKP1 + 10 ZKP4 + casts on a mid-range Android runs out of memory, or exceeds the foreground window.
findings.proposed_fix: Measure on the production validator droplet type and set a launch `max_delegates` (for example 10k) that keeps routing within budget. Benchmark ZKP4 batches on reference iOS and Android devices, with peak RSS. Measure real JSON sizes for the worst-case batch and set `max_vote_tx_bytes` from that. Add L7 (directory CDN at 50k wallets) and L8 (verifier spike with the 500/day cap) to the load matrix.
